**#148** — a pause mid-`move` repaints the panels with the new
quadrant's title over the old grid (`moving.c:123-136` sets the
coordinates, prints, and only then calls `newqad()`). Found by
`ui-review` here, pre-existing, verified in the source.

All four checks green, clean merge state.

**PR #149:** https://github.com/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/pull/149

## What #94 + #95 came to

The panels used to take 13 rows whatever the terminal had. Now they yield, and the conversation keeps a floor of three — two rows plus the line the prompt or pager sits on. At 16 rows and above nothing changes at all; below it the prompt is on screen down to four rows and a paged command actually shows something.

## Three things worth your attention

**The interesting part wasn't the fix — it was what the fix broke in the tests.** Three existing cases silently stopped testing anything when the geometry moved under them, each caught by a different pass:

| Stopped testing | Found by |
|---|---|
| the `maxy > 1` newline guard — *both* mutants passed the whole file | `verifier` |
| the panels' bottom border — the assertion was looking at the conversation | `code-review` |
| the two boundary panel heights, which moved to screens of 15 and 14 | `verifier` |

None of those lines was in my diff. Restoring the first also needed the case **reordered** to reach 5 rows straight from 24 — going via 15 rebuilds the pair where the guard is satisfied either way, so a broken build renders identically. I measured that rather than reasoned it.

**I damaged `sst.doc` and the `verifier` caught it.** My reflow scripts split a word (`a l  ine`) and ate a paragraph break. That's why both documents were reverted to `main` and re-applied by hand. A blunt tool on prose was the wrong call and it cost a FAIL verdict.

**The prose took four attempts.** Each of the first three contained a claim measurement contradicted — including one I took verbatim from a reviewer's own suggestion without re-deriving it, which turned out to be false. The final version scopes the rule to the case it holds for rather than naming another number. `code-review` ran eight times and requested changes on seven.

## Filed and left

**#148** — a pause mid-`move` repaints the panels with the new quadrant's title over the old grid. Pre-existing, verified in `moving.c:123-136`, found by `ui-review` here.

Two things I owe you as **unfiled**: `tui.c`'s scroll guard is uncovered in one direction (the gap predates this branch — `verifier` proved the same mutation survives on `main`), and `code-review` saw `[Transmission ends.]` when growing a *detached* tmux window past its creation width, reproducible on `main` too. The second may just be a harness artifact; I haven't confirmed it with a client attached.

S=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-scottdensmore-Developer-scottdensmore-super-star-trek/8bd691e1-6038-4f0d-82d9-378514dcc470/scratchpad
cat > $S/i5.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

Start the game with `-t` on a terminal smaller than 72x24. It says so
and falls back to the classic display, as it should. Resize the terminal
after that — grow it, shrink it, by one column — and **the game ends**:

```
 COMMAND> rest 5000
 Are you sure?
 [Transmission ends.]
 ****************************************
```

The question is never answered. Whatever the player had going is over,
with no confirmation and no chance to save.

## Why it is not just "resizing a classic game"

A game started **without** `-t` survives the same resize. Measured, same
seed, same command pending, 80x24 → 100x30:

| started as | after the resize |
| --- | --- |
| `sst tournament 7 short novice pw` | still at `Are you sure?`, game fine |
| `sst -t …` at 40x10 (fell back to classic) | `[Transmission ends.]`, game over |

So it is the **`-t` fallback path** specifically, not the classic
display in general. The difference is that `tui_init()` has already run
`initscr()` and then `endwin()` (`tui.c`, the `LINES < 24 || COLS < 72`
guard) before giving up, where a plain start never touches curses at
all. Something that leaves behind — the `SIGWINCH` disposition is the
obvious suspect — makes the next read return end-of-file, and `sst.c:674`
treats that as the player having gone away.

## How to see it

```sh
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch new-session -d -x 40 -y 10 -s t './build/debug/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw'
# "Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display."
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch send-keys -t t 'rest 5000' Enter
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch resize-window -t t -x 100 -y 30
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch capture-pane -t t -p
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch kill-server
```

Your own socket (`-L`) as above, never the default one, and never a bare
`tmux kill-server`.

Reproduces at 40x10, 40x24, 72x10 — any start below 72x24 — and on any
resize, including 40x10 → 41x11. It does **not** depend on how far the
terminal grows, which is what first made it look like a wide-terminal
problem.

## Scope

Pre-existing. Reproduced identically on `main` at ab4b6fd and on the
branch for #94/#95, so no recent display work causes it.

Reachable by an ordinary player: open a small terminal, start the game,
notice it is cramped, and make the window bigger — which is the natural
response to the message the game just printed telling you the terminal
is too small. The fallback exists to keep the player playing; ending
their game the moment they act on its advice is the opposite.

`sst.doc:1551` promises "Resizing the terminal never crashes the game
and never drops it back to the classic display, at any point". This is
neither of those literally, but it is worse than both, and the manual
gives a player no reason to expect it.

## Suggested approach

Find out what `initscr()`/`endwin()` leaves behind that a never-curses
start does not — `SIGWINCH` handling is the first place to look — and
either restore it when `tui_init()` gives up, or make the reader treat
an interrupted read as a retry rather than as end of input. The second
is probably right regardless: `EINTR` is not the player closing the
terminal, and `sst.c:674` cannot currently tell them apart.

Worth checking the other two fallback messages at `sst.c:463` and
`sst.c:465` at the same time — the no-terminal and cannot-address-cursor
paths reach the same place and may share the fault.

## Where it was found

Noticed by the `code-review` sub-agent while reviewing the #94/#95 fix,
as an aside it could not attribute and suspected was an artifact of
resizing a detached tmux window. It is not: it reproduces with any
resize, and the trigger is the sub-minimum start rather than the resize.
Characterised and filed separately per AGENTS.md step 9.

Follow the workflow in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).

## The one worth your attention

**#150** started as a throwaway aside — `code-review` mentioned `[Transmission ends.]` on a detached tmux resize and guessed it was a harness artifact. It isn't. Chasing it down: start `sst -t` on a terminal below 72x24, it falls back to the classic display as designed, and then **any** resize ends the game mid-question. A game started without `-t` survives the same resize, so it's the fallback path specifically — `initscr()`/`endwin()` having run leaves something behind that a plain start never touches.

A player hits this by doing exactly what the game's own message suggests: it says the terminal is too small, so they make the window bigger, and their game ends. Pre-existing on `main`, reachable in three steps.

## Honest note on how this went

The review passes earned their cost and then some — but the pattern in my own work was consistent and worth naming: **prose claims I hadn't measured.** The question-and-answer paragraph in `sst.doc` took four attempts, each of the first three containing something measurement contradicted, twice in text written to answer the previous round's finding about exactly that. Once I took a correction verbatim from a reviewer without re-deriving it and shipped its error into the docs.

I also damaged `sst.doc` with a bulk reflow script — a split word and a lost paragraph break — which cost a FAIL verdict and a revert. Blunt tooling on prose was the wrong call.

Three tests silently stopped testing anything when geometry moved under them, each caught by a different pass. None was in my diff. That's the failure mode this repo's workflow is built to catch, and it caught all three.

**Two loose ends from earlier that are still yours:** the 14 stray `build-*` directories (#146 covers the risk), and #141/#147/#151 as small, well-specified follow-ups if you want a shorter next slice.

# --- terminals the full-screen display cannot use --------------------
# Only a pty reaches these. The piped journey covers the no-terminal
# case; the terminfo probe and the size check need a real terminal that
# curses can ask about and still turn down. Each has to fall back to the
# classic display and keep playing rather than exit, hang, or draw a
# screen that never fills in.
#
# $1 description, $2 cols, $3 rows, $4 expected notice, $5 env prefix.
fallback() {
	start "$2" "$3" '' "$5"
	# Searched through the scrollback: the notice prints before the
	# banner, and on a 20-row terminal there is not much room between
	# them. A line added to the preamble later would push it off the
	# visible screen and turn this into a mystery.
	if ! wait_scrollback "$4"; then
		fail "$1: no notice that the full-screen display was refused"
		dump_scrollback
		return
	fi
	unwanted "$1: drew the panels on a terminal it had refused" " Quadrant "
	if ! wait_for 'regular, tournament, or frozen'; then
		fail "$1: the classic display did not carry on to a prompt"
		dump
		return
	fi
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'regular' Enter
	expect "$1: the classic display did not take an answer" 'Short, Medium, or Long'
}

# TERM=dumb is what Emacs' shell buffer sets: curses starts happily on
# it and then cannot address the cursor, so the game would look hung.
fallback "TERM=dumb" 80 24 "cannot do full-screen mode" 'env TERM=dumb'
# Smaller than the panels need. 72x24 is the floor; 70x20 is under it.
fallback "undersized terminal" 70 20 "Terminal too small" ''

if [ "$fails" -ne 0 ]; then
	printf '\n%d check(s) failed.\n' "$fails" >&2
	exit 1
fi

printf 'tui OK\n'

old = """	if (tui_active)
		got = tui_readline(buf, buflen);
	else
		got = fgets(buf, buflen, stdin) != NULL;

new = """	if (tui_active)
		got = tui_readline(buf, buflen);
	else {
		/* fgets says NULL for a read that was interrupted as well
		   as for one that reached the end of the input, and only
		   the second means no answer is ever coming. Telling them
		   apart is not hypothetical here: tui_init() runs initscr()
		   before it discovers the terminal is too small for the
		   panels, and endwin() does not take back the SIGWINCH
		   handler initscr() installed -- so once the game has
		   fallen back to the classic display, resizing the terminal
		   interrupts the read. It then ended the game mid-question,
		   which is what a player got for doing the obvious thing
		   about "Terminal too small (need 72x24)". Issue #150.
		   A game started without -t installs no handler and never
		   saw it, which is why this looked like a classic-display
		   fault and is not one.
		   feof() is the question worth asking; ferror() with EINTR
		   is the answer worth retrying. Anything else -- a real
		   read error -- still ends the session, as it did. */
		while ((got = fgets(buf, buflen, stdin) != NULL) == 0
		       && !feof(stdin) && errno == EINTR)

Start `sst -t` on a terminal smaller than 72x24. It prints "Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display." and falls back, as designed. Resize the terminal after that — grow it, shrink it, by one column — and the game **ends**:

```
 COMMAND> rest 5000
 Are you sure?
 [Transmission ends.]
```

The question is never answered. A player hits this by doing the obvious thing about the message the game just printed.

## Why

`readinput()` in `sst.c` reads the classic display with `fgets`, which returns NULL for an interrupted read as well as for end-of-input, and the session ends either way. `tui_init()` runs `initscr()` before it discovers the terminal is too small, and `endwin()` does not take back the `SIGWINCH` handler `initscr()` installed — so after the fallback a resize interrupts the read. A game started without `-t` installs no handler and survives the same resize.

I instrumented it at the failure point rather than reasoning: `feof(stdin)` 0, `ferror(stdin)` 1, `errno` 4 (`EINTR`).

## The fix

`readinput()` retries while the read was interrupted, and still ends the session on genuine end-of-input or any other error:

```c
while ((got = fgets(buf, buflen, stdin) != NULL) == 0
       && !feof(stdin) && errno == EINTR)
        clearerr(stdin);
```

## What I have checked

- The repro is fixed: the game survives, the question is still there, `n` answers it and returns to `COMMAND>`.
- Genuine EOF still ends the session — piped journeys and empty stdin both reach `[Transmission ends.]` and the sign-off; `tests/eof.sh` green.
- Plain mode byte-identical to `main` on a deterministic journey; full `ctest` 11/11.
- The new `tests/tui.sh` case fails on a build with the retry removed, with the intended message and nothing else.

## Please look hard at

1. **Whether the fallback game is genuinely usable after a resize now**, not merely alive. Play it: resize repeatedly, mid-question and mid-pause, grow and shrink, and see whether anything is garbled, doubled, or lost. The classic display has no repaint, so I want to know what a player actually sees.
2. **Whether a resize can now cost a keystroke or a line of input.** The retry re-enters `fgets` on the same buffer; I want to know if anything typed before the resize is lost or duplicated.
3. **The other two fallback notices** — `sst.c:463` (no terminal) and `sst.c:465` (terminal cannot address the cursor, e.g. `TERM=dumb`). They reach the same reader. Does the fix cover them, and is their behaviour sane on a resize?
4. **Whether ending on a real error is still right and still reachable** — the retry deliberately only covers `EINTR`.
5. Anything a player would trip over that no pass has named.

## 1. Verdict

**Acceptable as-is, with one should-fix on wording length.** Both fixes hold up under play. At a pause in the fallback game, growing, shrinking, and five rapid resizes in a row all leave the page and the `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` prompt exactly where they were, and the next Space still turns exactly one page; the `pause(1)` announcement (`[ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING...]`) likewise survives a resize and then delivers Uhura's message intact after the keystroke, screen-clear and all. A pending question survives a resize, and — better than the fix claims — a *partially typed* command survives one too (`srsc` + resize + `an` + Enter ran `srscan`). Nothing spins: 30 resizes cost the process 2 clock ticks. Plain mode and the real TUI are untouched, and EOF still ends the session cleanly rather than hanging in the new retry loop. The one thing I would change before merge is the reworded notice: at 75 characters it is now the longest of the three fallback notices and the only one that is *guaranteed* to print on a terminal too narrow to hold it, so the game's very first line now breaks mid-word on ordinary shapes such as 72x20.

## 2. Findings

**should-fix — `sst.c:465-472`, the reworded fallback notice wraps mid-word on the terminals it exists for.**
The new string is 75 columns:

```
Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using the classic display for this game.
```

Its two siblings in the same `if/else` are 63 and 70 columns — both fit the 72-column floor the message itself names. This one does not, and unlike them it only ever prints when the terminal is under 72 wide or under 24 tall. Measured in tmux:

- 72x20: `...classic display for this ga` / `me.`
- 74x20: `...for this game` / `.`
- 60x20: breaks at a space (`display` / `for this game.`) — lucky, not by design.

Of the widths 57-74 (all of which the *old* 57-column message rendered on one line), 26 now split mid-word. The comment that the change deleted — `/* Short: this one only ever prints on a narrow terminal. */` — was the guard against precisely this, and it went out with the rewording. A player's first impression of the game is a hyphen-less word break.

Suggestion: keep the new meaning but hold the line to ≤71 columns, e.g. `Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- classic display for this game.` (65), or `Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- classic display until restart.` (65), which additionally tells a player what *would* get them the panels. If the "for this game" nuance needs more room than that, print it as two `prout` lines so the game controls the break rather than the terminal:

```
Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display.
It stays classic for this game.
```

**nit — `sst.doc:1556-1559`, the new clause restates its neighbour and personifies the terminal.**
Two paragraphs above, at `sst.doc:1547-1549`, the manual already says "If the terminal is too small ... `-t` says so and plays in the classic display rather than failing." The new clause repeats that ("is told so and given the classic display") to reach the two genuinely new facts: that the choice lasts *for the game*, and that resizing is safe there. It is true as written and fits the 70-column measure, and putting the resize half in the resize paragraph is the right call. But "A terminal ... is told so" reads oddly when it is the player who is told, and the paragraph is happy to say "you" elsewhere ("It can still cost you one of the two"). Suggestion: move the durability half up to the fallback paragraph ("...and stays classic for the rest of the game"), and leave here only the part that belongs to resizing — "Resizing is safe in that classic display too, and neither answers a question nor turns a page for you."

**nit — `sst.c:465`, the longer notice costs two lines of a screen that has few.**
Related to the first finding rather than separate: on a 40x10 terminal the notice is now two lines of ten before the ASCII Enterprise scrolls it into the scrollback. `tests/tui.sh` already searches the scrollback for it and its comment acknowledges the squeeze. Shortening per the first finding fixes this too; no separate action needed.

**No finding — items 1, 4 and 5 of the ask came back clean.** Nothing skipped, doubled or cleared at any pause I could reach; no interaction between the two retries; nothing unresponsive; `SIGSTOP`/`SIGCONT` at a prompt is also survivable now.

My Python edit had rewritten `sst.c` from CRLF to LF wholesale: 960 CR bytes to zero, a 25-line fix inside a 1941-line diff. I reverted the file to `main` and re-applied the change as bytes. `sst.c` is CRLF again and `git diff --numstat sst.c` is 28 lines. `osx.c` is LF in `main` and still is.

- **5** — `sst.doc`'s resize paragraph gains a clause: a terminal too small at startup is told so and given the classic display for the game, resizing is safe there too, and neither answers a question nor turns a page.
- **6** — `errno = 0` before the read and again in the loop. The partial-fill case you describe is noted as unreachable in canonical mode and not guarded.

content.text:
## 1. Verdict

**Acceptable as-is, with one should-fix on wording length.** Both fixes hold up under play. At a pause in the fallback game, growing, shrinking, and five rapid resizes in a row all leave the page and the `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` prompt exactly where they were, and the next Space still turns exactly one page; the `pause(1)` announcement (`[ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING...]`) likewise survives a resize and then delivers Uhura's message intact after the keystroke, screen-clear and all. A pending question survives a resize, and — better than the fix claims — a *partially typed* command survives one too (`srsc` + resize + `an` + Enter ran `srscan`). Nothing spins: 30 resizes cost the process 2 clock ticks. Plain mode and the real TUI are untouched, and EOF still ends the session cleanly rather than hanging in the new retry loop. The one thing I would change before merge is the reworded notice: at 75 characters it is now the longest of the three fallback notices and the only one that is *guaranteed* to print on a terminal too narrow to hold it, so the game's very first line now breaks mid-word on ordinary shapes such as 72x20.

## 2. Findings

**should-fix — `sst.c:465-472`, the reworded fallback notice wraps mid-word on the terminals it exists for.**
The new string is 75 columns:

```
Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using the classic display for this game.
```

Its two siblings in the same `if/else` are 63 and 70 columns — both fit the 72-column floor the message itself names. This one does not, and unlike them it only ever prints when the terminal is under 72 wide or under 24 tall. Measured in tmux:

- 72x20: `...classic display for this ga` / `me.`
- 74x20: `...for this game` / `.`
- 60x20: breaks at a space (`display` / `for this game.`) — lucky, not by design.

Of the widths 57-74 (all of which the *old* 57-column message rendered on one line), 26 now split mid-word. The comment that the change deleted — `/* Short: this one only ever prints on a narrow terminal. */` — was the guard against precisely this, and it went out with the rewording. A player's first impression of the game is a hyphen-less word break.

Suggestion: keep the new meaning but hold the line to ≤71 columns, e.g. `Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- classic display for this game.` (65), or `Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- classic display until restart.` (65), which additionally tells a player what *would* get them the panels. If the "for this game" nuance needs more room than that, print it as two `prout` lines so the game controls the break rather than the terminal:

```
Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display.
It stays classic for this game.
```

**nit — `sst.doc:1556-1559`, the new clause restates its neighbour and personifies the terminal.**
Two paragraphs above, at `sst.doc:1547-1549`, the manual already says "If the terminal is too small ... `-t` says so and plays in the classic display rather than failing." The new clause repeats that ("is told so and given the classic display") to reach the two genuinely new facts: that the choice lasts *for the game*, and that resizing is safe there. It is true as written and fits the 70-column measure, and putting the resize half in the resize paragraph is the right call. But "A terminal ... is told so" reads oddly when it is the player who is told, and the paragraph is happy to say "you" elsewhere ("It can still cost you one of the two"). Suggestion: move the durability half up to the fallback paragraph ("...and stays classic for the rest of the game"), and leave here only the part that belongs to resizing — "Resizing is safe in that classic display too, and neither answers a question nor turns a page for you."

**nit — `sst.c:465`, the longer notice costs two lines of a screen that has few.**
Related to the first finding rather than separate: on a 40x10 terminal the notice is now two lines of ten before the ASCII Enterprise scrolls it into the scrollback. `tests/tui.sh` already searches the scrollback for it and its comment acknowledges the squeeze. Shortening per the first finding fixes this too; no separate action needed.

**No finding — items 1, 4 and 5 of the ask came back clean.** Nothing skipped, doubled or cleared at any pause I could reach; no interaction between the two retries; nothing unresponsive; `SIGSTOP`/`SIGCONT` at a prompt is also survivable now.

## 3. What I exercised

Build: `cmake --preset debug && cmake --build --preset debug`.

Plain mode (no `-t`), piped:
- `regular/short/novice/xyz/srscan/quit/n` — banner, setup, SRSCAN, quit all read correctly.
- Input truncated mid-question (`rest 5000` then EOF) and at a pause (`help move` then EOF) — both end with `[Transmission ends.]` and the closing benediction, no hang, exit 0. The new `feof`/`EINTR` loop does not trap at end of input.

- 60x20 → `help move` → resize to 100x30 during the pause: page and prompt unchanged. Then shrink to 50x16 during the pause: unchanged. Space: exactly one page advanced. Five rapid resizes (72x24, 60x18, 100x30, 40x12, 80x24) at a pause: unchanged, Space still advances one page. Paged to the end, back to `COMMAND>`.
- 40x10 → `rest 5000` → `Are you sure?` → grow to 100x30: no `[Transmission ends.]`; `n` then `srscan` printed a live scan with `Time Left 7.00`.
- 60x18 emeritus (`tournament 42 long emeritus pw`) → `rest 3` → `[ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING...]` (`pause(1)`) → grow to 100x30: announcement still pending; Space then delivered Uhura's starbase-under-attack message and Spock's question; resize to 72x24 during *that* question, answered `y`, rest cancelled correctly.
- Partial input: typed `srsc` (no Enter), resized 60x18→100x30, typed `an` + Enter — `srscan` ran. The typed characters are not lost.
- CPU: 30 resizes across widths 70-109 and heights 14-29 cost the process 2 clock ticks; `srscan` answered afterwards.
- `SIGSTOP` then `SIGCONT` at a `COMMAND>` prompt: game survives and answers `status`.
- 70x22 journey: `srscan`, `lrscan`, `chart`, `status`, `damages`, `move 1 5`, resize to 90x26, `chart` (grid aligned), `quit` → resize during the slow-printed star rule (rendered complete, 54 stars) → `Do you want your score recorded?` `y` → filename → `Do you want to play again?` `n`.
- Notice rendering captured at 40x10, 60x20, 72x20, 74x20, plus a computed wrap table for widths 20-80.

Full-screen mode (regression check): 80x24 panels render correctly; shrink to 60x16 clips with `>` and keeps playing; grow back to 80x24 redraws. Unaffected by this change, as expected — both retries sit on the non-TUI side of `tui_active`.

Builds go through `CMakePresets.json`: `cmake --preset ci-debug`, `ctest --preset ci-debug` / `ci-release`.

## The change (issue #150)

Start `sst -t` on a terminal under 72x24. It falls back to the classic display, as designed. Resize afterwards — any direction, any amount — and the game **ended** mid-question with `[Transmission ends.]`.

`tui_init()` runs `initscr()` before it discovers the terminal is too small, and `endwin()` does not take back the `SIGWINCH` handler `initscr()` installed. So after the fallback a resize interrupts the read. Both readers then misread that:

- `readinput()` (`sst.c`) used `fgets(...) != NULL`, which is false for an interrupted read as well as for end-of-input, and ended the session either way. Instrumented at the failure: `feof` 0, `ferror` 1, `errno` 4 (`EINTR`).
- `getch()` (`osx.c`) used `read(0, &chbuf, 1) != 1`, so an interrupted read came back as a keypress — a resize answered `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` and took the page with it. `ui-review` found this second one; `sst.doc:1551-1553` promises against both in one sentence.

Both now retry on `EINTR` only; genuine EOF and any other error still end the session exactly as before.

Also: the "Terminal too small" notice is reworded (and kept to 65 columns, since it is the one notice that only ever prints on a terminal under 72 wide), and `sst.doc` gains a clause.

## What I have run

- `ci-debug` and `debug` build clean; `tests/tui.sh` green; `tests/eof.sh` green; `tests/help.sh` green; full `ctest --preset ci-debug` 11/11.
- Genuine EOF still ends the session: piped journeys, empty stdin, and `0<&-` all reach `[Transmission ends.]` and the sign-off, exit 0, no hang.
- Plain mode byte-identical to `main` on a deterministic journey.
- Two new `tests/tui.sh` cases, each proved against its own mutant: removing `readinput`'s retry fails `resize fallback:` alone; removing `getch`'s fails `resize pause:` alone.

## Please cover at your own scope, and specifically

1. **`ctest` in both `ci-*` presets**, goldens included.
2. **That neither retry can spin or hang.** They are unbounded `EINTR` loops on a terminal read. `ui-review` measured 30 resizes costing 2 clock ticks, but a signal storm, `SIGSTOP`/`SIGCONT`, and a closed stdin are worth your own look.
3. **That genuine end-of-input and real errors still end the session** — this is what `readinput()` exists for and what `tests/eof.sh` and the journey tests depend on. If EOF ever stopped ending the game the suite would hang rather than fail, so please check it deliberately rather than by the suite passing.
4. **Whether the `resize pause:` case is blind.** It took three attempts to make fail: a pause prompt on screen afterwards proves nothing (an answered pause prints the next page and stops at its own prompt), and asking whether a remembered line is still *somewhere* on screen proves nothing either (the terminal grew, so the old page is scrolled up rather than gone). ## Verdict: request changes

Reviewed state: branch `fix/resize-ends-fallback-game` at `246c6f5` (no commits; `git diff main...HEAD` empty, nothing staged). Pending worktree changes only: modified `sst.c`, `osx.c`, `sst.doc`, `tests/tui.sh`. No untracked files.

I built the worktree in a scratch copy (`cmake --preset debug` and `ci-debug`, zero warnings under `-Werror`), and drove both new cases by hand in a private tmux socket against both the worktree build and a `git archive main` build. The fix is real and the tests are not blind to the bug they were written for: on the `main` build the resize produced `[Transmission ends.]` under `Are you sure?`, and the pause marker moved from `command to move one sector to the right would be` to `moving within a quadrant, <qrow> and <qcol> may be omitted. For`; on the worktree build neither happens. I also confirmed a part-typed answer (`n` with no Enter) survives the resize and is still accepted, and that EOF, `< /dev/null`, `0<&-` (EBADF) and `< /home` (EISDIR) all still reach `[Transmission ends.]` and the sign-off with rc 0 and no spin. The two retry loops are correct and terminating: `getch()` only inspects `errno` when `n < 0`, where it is guaranteed set; `readinput()` sets `errno = 0` both before and inside the loop and gates on `!feof(stdin)`, so an EOF that leaves `errno` untouched cannot be mistaken for `EINTR`, and `clearerr()` is in the right place (reached only when `!feof`, so it clears the error indicator and not a pending EOF). Nothing here is a correctness blocker.

### Findings

**should-fix — review coverage: no claim that the last `ui-review` round saw this state, and the narrative suggests it did not.**
The diff plainly reaches the player: `sst.c:481-482` now prints a second line on the first screen a fallback player sees, and both readers change what a resize does to a pending question and a pager. You reported `ui-review` twice and `verifier` once, but not the fact step 8 asks for — whether the last `ui-review` round saw the state being committed. Your own account reads the other way: the last `ui-review` saw a 65-column single-line notice, the `verifier` then showed the gate is `LINES < 24 || COLS < 72`, and *hence* the two short lines that are in the tree now. That is new player-visible text created after the pass that would have read it, which is exactly the rerun step 6 requires. Please state the last `ui-review`'s verdict and the list of screens it says it exercised, and if the two-line notice postdates it, rerun `ui-review` on this state before committing.

**should-fix — `tests/tui.sh:2793` and `tests/tui.sh:2864`: neither new case checks that the resize actually landed, so both pass vacuously if it does not.**
Every other resize in this file is followed by a positive assertion about the new geometry (e.g. `tests/tui.sh:590-594` measures the top line's width), which fails loudly if `resize-window` did nothing. These two assert only that nothing happened — if `tm resize-window` errors (an older tmux without the command, a `window-size` state that refuses it, a session that died), stderr goes nowhere the script reads, `lastline` is unchanged, `Transmission ends` is absent, and both cases report green while never delivering a `SIGWINCH`. The same gap covers the fixed `sleep 1`: a resize that has not taken effect within a second is indistinguishable from one that caused nothing. Suggested fix: after each resize, poll until the pane really is the new size before asserting — e.g. loop on `[ "$(tm display-message -p -t "$pane" '#{pane_width}')" = 100 ]` and `fail` on timeout, which also replaces the fixed sleep with a wait for the event you are testing.

**should-fix — `sst.c:472-474`: the comment's claim about wrapping is contradicted by the output.**
"One long sentence would wrap mid-word somewhere, on the very first line the player sees; two short ones wrap nowhere sensible" is not what the two lines do. Only the second is short; the first is 57 columns and is broken by the terminal, mid-word, on the very first line the player sees. Measured on this build at 50x10:

```
Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic d
isplay.
It stays classic until you restart.
```

(at 40 columns it happens to break at the space, which is luck, not the game breaking it). What is true is that the *added* sentence was given its own line rather than lengthening a line that already wraps. Given this change's history of comment claims that did not survive measurement, please reword to that. The 57-column first line is pre-existing and belongs in an issue under step 9, not in this slice.

**nit — `sst.c:685-686`: the comment names a function the code does not call.**
"feof() is the question worth asking; ferror() with EINTR is the answer worth retrying" — the loop tests `!feof(stdin) && errno == EINTR` and never calls `ferror()`. It is the right test; the sentence sends the next reader looking for a call that is not there. Say `errno` where you mean `errno`.

**nit — `sst.doc:1548-1549` understates the scope, and `README.md:97` was not updated.**
`tui_init()` is called once in `main()` (`sst.c:462`) before the play-again loop, so a second game started from the play-again prompt is classic too — "stays classic for the rest of the game" reads as if a new game might get the panels back. The on-screen notice ("until you restart") is right; "for the rest of the session" would match it. Separately, `README.md:97` still describes the fallback with no mention of it being permanent, and that paragraph is the README's whole treatment of this behaviour.

**nit — `tests/tui.sh:2805-2812`: case 1 proves the game is alive, not that the question survived.**
If a future regression made the resize abort the pending question but leave the game running (an empty answer taken as the answer, say), `n` would be read as a command, `Beg your pardon, Captain?` would print, `srscan` would still show `Time Left`, and the case would pass — while the game had done exactly what `sst.doc:1558-1560` now promises it does not ("neither answers a question"). A cheap strengthening: after the resize, assert `Beg your pardon` is absent and that `Are you sure` is not asked a second time.

**nit — the cause is still installed; only the two readers are hardened.**
`tui.c:996-999` calls `endwin()` and returns FALSE without `delscreen()` and without restoring `SIGWINCH`, so the handler outlives the fallback for the whole session. The retries make the two readers immune, which is the more general fix (it covers `SIGTSTP`/`SIGCONT` too), but any other interruptible blocking call in the classic path stays exposed — notably a stdio write to a tty that blocks, where glibc latches the error indicator and the game goes quiet. I could not construct that failure, so this is not a request to change the fix; it is worth an issue under step 9, or one `signal(SIGWINCH, SIG_DFL)` beside that `endwin()`.

### Not reviewed / caveats

- I did not run the full `ctest` battery or the golden fixtures; that is the `verifier`'s scope and you reported it PASS in both `ci-*` presets. I did rebuild both presets to confirm the diff compiles warning-free under `-Werror`.
- macOS/BSD `fgets` differs from glibc when a read is interrupted after partial data (it returns the partial line as if complete rather than NULL). I judged it unreachable here — the tty is in canonical mode, so a line is delivered whole or not at all, and the only path that installs the handler requires a tty — but I could not test on macOS.
- Line endings check out: `sst.c` 998/998 and `sst.doc` 1673/1673 CRLF, `osx.c` and `tests/tui.sh` pure LF, no trailing whitespace introduced, and `osx.c`'s missing final newline is unchanged from `main`.

## Verdict: request changes

Reviewed state: branch `fix/resize-ends-fallback-game` at `246c6f5` (no commits; `git diff main...HEAD` empty, nothing staged). Pending worktree changes only: modified `sst.c`, `osx.c`, `sst.doc`, `tests/tui.sh`. No untracked files.

The fix is real and the tests are not blind to the bug they were written for: on the `main` build the resize produced `[Transmission ends.]` under `Are you sure?`, and the pause marker moved from `command to move one sector to the right would be` to `moving within a quadrant, <qrow> and <qcol> may be omitted. For`; on the worktree build neither happens. I also confirmed a part-typed answer (`n` with no Enter) survives the resize and is still accepted, and that EOF, `< /dev/null`, `0<&-` (EBADF) and `< /home` (EISDIR) all still reach `[Transmission ends.]` and the sign-off with rc 0 and no spin. The two retry loops are correct and terminating: `getch()` only inspects `errno` when `n < 0`, where it is guaranteed set; `readinput()` sets `errno = 0` both before and inside the loop and gates on `!feof(stdin)`, so an EOF that leaves `errno` untouched cannot be mistaken for `EINTR`, and `clearerr()` is in the right place (reached only when `!feof`, so it clears the error indicator and not a pending EOF). Nothing here is a correctness blocker.

### Findings

**should-fix — review coverage: no claim that the last `ui-review` round saw this state, and the narrative suggests it did not.**
The diff plainly reaches the player: `sst.c:481-482` now prints a second line on the first screen a fallback player sees, and both readers change what a resize does to a pending question and a pager. You reported `ui-review` twice and `verifier` once, but not the fact step 8 asks for — whether the last `ui-review` round saw the state being committed. Your own account reads the other way: the last `ui-review` saw a 65-column single-line notice, the `verifier` then showed the gate is `LINES < 24 || COLS < 72`, and *hence* the two short lines that are in the tree now. That is new player-visible text created after the pass that would have read it, which is exactly the rerun step 6 requires. Please state the last `ui-review`'s verdict and the list of screens it says it exercised, and if the two-line notice postdates it, rerun `ui-review` on this state before committing.

**should-fix — `tests/tui.sh:2793` and `tests/tui.sh:2864`: neither new case checks that the resize actually landed, so both pass vacuously if it does not.**
Every other resize in this file is followed by a positive assertion about the new geometry (e.g. `tests/tui.sh:590-594` measures the top line's width), which fails loudly if `resize-window` did nothing. These two assert only that nothing happened — if `tm resize-window` errors (an older tmux without the command, a `window-size` state that refuses it, a session that died), stderr goes nowhere the script reads, `lastline` is unchanged, `Transmission ends` is absent, and both cases report green while never delivering a `SIGWINCH`. isplay.

What is true is that the *added* sentence was given its own line rather than lengthening a line that already wraps. Given this change's history of comment claims that did not survive measurement, please reword to that. The 57-column first line is pre-existing and belongs in an issue under step 9, not in this slice.

**nit — `sst.c:685-686`: the comment names a function the code does not call.**
"feof() is the question worth asking; ferror() with EINTR is the answer worth retrying" — the loop tests `!feof(stdin) && errno == EINTR` and never calls `ferror()`. It is the right test; the sentence sends the next reader looking for a call that is not there. Say `errno` where you mean `errno`.

`tui_init()` is called once in `main()` (`sst.c:462`) before the play-again loop, so a second game started from the play-again prompt is classic too — "stays classic for the rest of the game" reads as if a new game might get the panels back. The on-screen notice ("until you restart") is right; "for the rest of the session" would match it. Separately, `README.md:97` still describes the fallback with no mention of it being permanent, and that paragraph is the README's whole treatment of this behaviour.

**nit — `tests/tui.sh:2805-2812`: case 1 proves the game is alive, not that the question survived.**
If a future regression made the resize abort the pending question but leave the game running (an empty answer taken as the answer, say), `n` would be read as a command, `Beg your pardon, Captain?` would print, `srscan` would still show `Time Left`, and the case would pass — while the game had done exactly what `sst.doc:1558-1560` now promises it does not ("neither answers a question"). A cheap strengthening: after the resize, assert `Beg your pardon` is absent and that `Are you sure` is not asked a second time.

**nit — the cause is still installed; only the two readers are hardened.**
`tui.c:996-999` calls `endwin()` and returns FALSE without `delscreen()` and without restoring `SIGWINCH`, so the handler outlives the fallback for the whole session. The retries make the two readers immune, which is the more general fix (it covers `SIGTSTP`/`SIGCONT` too), but any other interruptible blocking call in the classic path stays exposed — notably a stdio write to a tty that blocks, where glibc latches the error indicator and the game goes quiet. I could not construct that failure, so this is not a request to change the fix; it is worth an issue under step 9, or one `signal(SIGWINCH, SIG_DFL)` beside that `endwin()`.

## Problem

`tui_init()` calls `initscr()` before it can know whether the terminal
is big enough for the panels, and on finding it is not it calls
`endwin()` and returns FALSE:

```c
	initscr();
	if (LINES < 24 || COLS < 72) {
		endwin();
		return FALSE;
	}
```

`endwin()` does not undo what `initscr()` installed. ncurses' `SIGWINCH`
handler outlives the fallback, for the whole session, in a game that is
now running on the classic display and has no use for it.

## Why it matters

It made every blocking read in the classic path interruptible where a
game started without `-t` has nothing to interrupt it. That was #150:
`readinput()` read the interrupted read as end-of-input and ended the
game, and `getch()` read it as a keypress and answered a pause. Both are
fixed by retrying on `EINTR`, which is the more general remedy — it
covers `SIGTSTP`/`SIGCONT` too — but it hardens the two readers rather
than removing the cause.

Anything else in the classic path that blocks is still exposed. The one
worth naming is a stdio *write* to a tty that blocks: glibc latches the
stream's error indicator on `EINTR`, and the game would go quiet with no
diagnostic. Found by `code-review` while reviewing #150; it could not
construct that failure and neither could I, which is why this is a
separate issue rather than part of that fix.

## Suggested approach

One line beside the `endwin()`:

```c
	signal(SIGWINCH, SIG_DFL);
```

`SIG_DFL` for `SIGWINCH` is "ignore", which is what a classic game wants
and what it would have had if `-t` had never been passed.

Worth checking whether `delscreen()` belongs there too — `initscr()`
allocates a `SCREEN` that nothing frees on this path — and whether the
retries in `readinput()` and `getch()` should stay once the handler is
gone. They should: they cost nothing, they are correct regardless, and
they cover signals this does not.

## How to see it

The observable consequences are fixed, so this needs reading rather than
running: `tui.c`'s `tui_init()` for the `endwin()` without a matching
restore, and `sst.c`'s `readinput()` and `osx.c`'s `getch()` for the
retries that now stand in its place.

## Where it was found

By `code-review` while reviewing the fix for #150, as the observation
that the fix hardens the readers rather than removing what makes them
need hardening. Filed rather than folded in, per AGENTS.md step 9 — the
retries are the right fix for the readers, and this is a different
change to a different file.

Follow the workflow in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).

cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
S=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-scottdensmore-Developer-scottdensmore-super-star-trek/8bd691e1-6038-4f0d-82d9-378514dcc470/scratchpad
cat > $S/i9.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

The full-screen decision is made once, at startup, and never revisited.
`tui_init()` is called at `sst.c:462`, before the play-again loop that
begins at `sst.c:522`. So a player who starts on a terminal too small
for the panels, enlarges it, finishes the game and answers yes to "Do
you want to play again?" gets **another classic game** — on a terminal
that would now hold the panels perfectly well.

Nothing says so at that moment. The notice printed at startup has long
since scrolled away, and the second game simply begins without panels.

## Why it is worth doing now

Before #150 nobody reached this: enlarging the terminal ended the game
outright, so there was no play-again prompt to answer. Fixing that made
the sequence — enlarge, finish, play again — an ordinary thing a player
can do, and it is the sequence most likely to follow the message telling
them the terminal is too small.

`sst.doc` and `README.md` were extended in that change to say the choice
lasts for the session, and the on-screen notice now says "restart sst at
72x24 to get the panels". Those are honest descriptions of a limitation
rather than of a decision anyone made. Retrying would let all three say
something better.

## How to see it

```sh
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch new-session -d -x 70 -y 20 -s t './build/debug/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw'
# "Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display."
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch send-keys -t t 'quit' Enter
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch resize-window -t t -x 100 -y 30
# answer the score question, then "Do you want to play again?" with y
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch capture-pane -t t -p     # classic, no panels, no notice
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch kill-server
```

Your own socket (`-L`) as above, never the default one, and never a bare
`tmux kill-server`.

## Suggested approach

Two sizes of answer, and the smaller may be enough:

- **Reprint the notice** for a second game that is still classic, so the
  player is told rather than left to notice. Cheap, and it makes the
  current behaviour honest.
- **Retry `tui_init()`** per game. Better for the player, but it needs
  care: the panels' state, `tui_active`, and what happens if the second
  attempt fails where the first succeeded (a terminal shrunk between
  games) all have to be worked out, and `tui_shutdown()` is currently
  wired to `atexit` and to `tui_gameover()`.

Whichever, `sst.doc:1547-1550`, `README.md`'s fallback paragraph and the
second line of the startup notice all describe the present behaviour and
would need to move with it.

## Where it was found

By the `ui-review` sub-agent while reviewing the fix for #150, as the
player action that fix newly makes possible. Filed rather than folded in
per AGENTS.md step 9 — #150 is about two readers misreading an
interrupted read, and this is a different decision in a different place.

Follow the workflow in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF
gh issue create --title "The classic-display choice is never revisited, so a second game stays classic" --body-file $S/i9.md 2>&1 | tail -1

## Verdict: request changes

Reviewed state: worktree at `246c6f5` (no commits on the branch, `git diff main...HEAD` empty), with modifications to `sst.c`, `osx.c`, `sst.doc`, `README.md`, `tests/tui.sh` — the #150 EINTR retry in `readinput()` and `getch()`, the two-line fallback notice, the doc/README session-scope wording, and two new `tui.sh` cases. No untracked files, no staged changes.

The C fix itself I found sound. I re-built the worktree in a copy outside the repo (`-DSST_WERROR=ON`, clean), drove the pause scenario by hand in a private tmux, and checked the reachable failure modes of both readers. Two things below need answering before commit.

### Findings

**should-fix — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh:2838-2840`: the guard that was added to close the "the resize answered the question" gap cannot fire, for two independent reasons.**

The failure mode the comment at 2820-2824 describes does not produce `Beg your pardon`. `ja()` (`sst.c:778-787`) loops until it sees `y` or `n`; an empty answer makes it print `Please answer with "Y" or "N":` and read again — it never returns to the command prompt, so `n` is consumed as the answer, not as a command. Your own README says exactly this at `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/README.md:91-92`. Confirmed against the build: `printf 'regular\nshort\nnovice\nxyz\nrest 5000\n\nn\n...' | ./build/sst` prints `Are you sure?` then `Please answer with "Y" or "N":`, and never `Beg your pardon`.

So a build in which the resize injected an empty line would pass this case entirely: `Transmission ends` absent (pass), `Are you sure` still on screen exactly once — `ja()` does not reprint the question (pass), `Beg your pardon` absent (pass), `srscan` → `Time Left` (pass). The one observable that separates the two worlds is `Please answer`, and nothing looks for it.

Second, the check is run immediately after `send-keys`, with no intervening poll, so it samples the screen before the game can have responded — the file's own idiom elsewhere waits for the response first (`tui.sh:495-496` after `wait_for`, `tui.sh:2616-2617` after `expect_re`).

Suggested fix: assert `Please answer` is absent, and place the absence checks after the polling `expect ... 'Time Left'`, e.g.

```sh
tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'n' Enter
tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'srscan' Enter
expect "resize fallback: the game stopped answering after the resize" 'Time Left'
unwanted "resize fallback: the resize answered the question with an empty line" 'Please answer'
```

At 100x30 the `Please answer` line is still on screen after `srscan` output, so ordering it last costs nothing. The comment at 2820-2824 needs correcting with it, since it is the premise the check rests on.

**should-fix — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:491`: the last `ui-review` round did not see the string being committed.**

By your own account the pass returned "acceptable with one should-fix on wording" and you then changed the printed text to `It stays classic: restart sst at 72x24 to get the panels.`. That is a change to what the game shows a player made *after* the pass reported, which is the case AGENTS.md step 6 names explicitly ("If fixing one changes what the game shows a player, rerun `ui-review` on the result"), and the case step 8 has me check for. Everything else in the diff was covered by a run whose stated coverage — notice at twelve widths, the 72x24 boundary, the #150 scenario, the pause fix in both directions, a part-typed answer, plain mode — does match what the diff can reach; this one line is the gap.

It is a narrow rerun (the notice at 40-100 columns and at 23/18/17 rows, nothing else printed changed). Alternatively resolve it explicitly — e.g. if `ui-review` itself dictated this exact sentence, say so — and record that in the summary/PR body per "Answering a finding". What I cannot do is treat it as covered.

**nit — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:698-702`: the retry can silently drop a partially read line, which the new absolute in `sst.doc` does not allow for.**

glibc's `fgets` returns NULL when the stream errors even if it had already copied bytes into `buf` (`count > 0 && _IO_ERR_SEEN && errno != EAGAIN`), and those bytes are gone from the stream; the retry then restarts at `buf[0]`. Reaching it needs the stdio buffer to be partially filled when the signal lands, which in canonical mode means something like Ctrl-D mid-line followed by a resize — contrived, and not a regression (the old code ended the session there). Worth a sentence in the comment noting the limit, or nothing at all if you judge it unreachable; I would not restructure the loop for it.

**nit — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh:2894-2900`: the pause case's marker depends on the first `help move` page ending on a line that fits in 60 columns.**

I verified today that it does: at 60x20 the last content line is `command to move one sector to the right would be`, and growing to 100x30 reflows the wrapped lines above it without changing that one, so `lastline` matches. But if the paragraph shifts so the page ends on a wrap fragment, tmux's reflow on the width change joins it and the comparison fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the fix. The failure is loud, not silent, so this is only maintenance risk. If you want it out: `tm resize-window -t "$session" -x 60 -y 30` delivers the same SIGWINCH with no width change and therefore no reflow.

### What I could not review

- I did not run the full `tui.sh`, `ctest`, or the golden battery — that is the `verifier`'s scope, and you report it green plus a control run of the branch's `tui.sh` against a `main`-built binary failing exactly the two new cases, which is the right evidence for non-vacuity of the cases as wholes (it does not, however, cover the `Beg your pardon` guard inside case 1, which the control cannot distinguish since the case fails on the first check).
- macOS and non-glibc libc behaviour of `fgets`/`errno` on EINTR; I checked the glibc path and the code's `feof`-first structure is correct on any conforming libc.

**1 — fixed, and the premise checks out.** `sst.c:785-794` is exactly as you describe: `ja()` loops on `scan()`/`chew()` and prints `Please answer with "Y" or "N":` (line 792) for anything that is not `y`/`n`, so `Beg your pardon` (line 928) is unreachable from there. `scan()` does `*citem = 0` on entry (sst.c:743), so an empty line cannot be answered by a stale `citem` — the observable really is printed on the empty-answer path, which is what makes the guard able to fire. Placement after `expect ... Documentation, not a screen.

**3 — resolved as agreed.** The comment states the limit, why canonical mode puts it out of reach, and that the old code ended the session there. The loop itself is sound: `(got = fgets(...) != NULL) == 0 && !feof(stdin) && errno == EINTR`, with `errno` cleared before each attempt and `clearerr()` inside — a non-`EINTR` failure and EOF both fall out with `got == 0` and end the session exactly as before, and a game without `-t` installs no handler so plain mode and the golden recordings cannot see any of it.

Fine to resolve by pointing at the control run.

I did not re-run `tests/tui.sh` or the builds — I took your green run and the `main`-binary control on trust, having confirmed the two new cases fail loudly rather than silently when a resize does not land, which is what would make a green run meaningful. Everything else above I checked against the source.

Approved — go ahead and commit with `Closes #150`.

fix: do not read a resize as the player going away

Closes #150.

Start sst -t on a terminal under 72x24. It says the terminal is too
small, falls back to the classic display, and keeps playing -- which is
what the fallback is for. Resize the terminal after that, in either
direction, by any amount, and the game ended mid-question:

    COMMAND> rest 5000
    Are you sure?
    [Transmission ends.]

A player reaches that by doing the obvious thing about the message the
game has just printed.

tui_init() runs initscr() before it can know the terminal is too small,
and endwin() does not take back the SIGWINCH handler initscr()

question cost **0 clock ticks**.

it they wait for panels that are not coming — the choice is made once at
startup, so even a second game from the play-again prompt is classic. So

## Session total

**Six issues closed across five merged PRs:**

| | |
|---|---|
| `3e0c97f` | **#90** — stale columns outside every curses window |
| `4fe5088` | **#125** — `CMakePresets.json` as the one place the build is defined |

**Ten issues filed** — #141, #145, #146, #147, #148, #150 (since closed), #151, #152, #153, #154 — each verified against the code before filing rather than passed along.

## The through-line

The last two slices were connected in a way I didn't expect. Fixing #94/#95 made the short-terminal band usable, which is what let `ui-review` reach the fallback game and stumble over `[Transmission ends.]` — first reported as a probable tmux artifact. Chasing that down produced #150, whose fix then made "enlarge, finish, play again" an ordinary thing a player can do, which is #154. Each fix opened the door to the next finding.

## Where I'd point you next

**#152** is the honest completion of what just landed: the retries harden two readers, but `endwin()` still leaves the `SIGWINCH` handler installed, so anything else interruptible in the classic path stays exposed. It's a one-line fix with a real question attached (whether `delscreen()` belongs there too).

**#153** is a one-line `.gitignore` addition — genuinely five minutes.

**#141** and **#89** remain the best contained, player-facing options.

## One thing worth your judgement

My own recurring failure this session was **asserting things in prose I hadn't measured** — three successive justification comments in #150 alone, and four attempts at one `sst.doc` paragraph in #94/#95. Twice a bulk Python reflow also damaged a file (a split word, a lost paragraph break, a wholesale CRLF→LF conversion).

The review passes caught every instance, which is the system working. But if you want fewer rounds per slice, the cheapest lever is probably a rule that a comment stating a number or a threshold has to name how it was measured — the same discipline AGENTS.md already applies to tests via the mutation proof. That's your call, not mine to add.

content.text:
Yes — but narrowly, and not as a new rule.

## Why it's worth doing

The failure mode isn't that the discipline is missing from this repo. Step 4 already owns it for tests: *a claim has to be able to fail, so break it and write down what you broke.* The gap is that it stops at tests, while this codebase treats **comments as specification** — every review pass this session read them as the reason the code is the way it is, and disputed them on those terms.

The strongest evidence isn't the error count. It's that by round three of #150 I was hand-writing *"check the comment claims, every round has found one"* into the reviewer briefs. That's a rule being re-invented per session — precisely what AGENTS.md's own preamble says the file exists to stop: "an improvised reviewer drifts."

## What I'd add — one paragraph, attached to step 4

Not a new section. Extending the section that already owns the principle costs less and drifts less:

> A comment that states a number is a claim like any other, and here comments are read as specification — the review passes take them as the reason the code is the way it is. Say where the number came from: measured on screen at 72x14, counted in `reports.c`, derived from `PANELH`. A claim carrying its source is one the next reader checks in a minute; one without it they must trust or re-derive.
>
> Not a call for precision in general. It is about the sentence that says *why* — a threshold, a width, a count of rows. Those are what a later change quietly falsifies and what a reviewer cannot dispute without redoing the work. In one session several such claims did not survive checking, twice inside text written to answer the previous round's finding about exactly that.

Phrased as **disclosure**, deliberately: "say where it came from" is checkable by the next reader. "Be accurate" is an aspiration and would rot.

## The honest case against

Three real objections, and you should weigh them:

- **The file is 567 lines** and its own tracker says it accretes — #110 is literally about this section being gutted silently, #138 about a factual error in it. Adding to it has a cost.
- **Every instance was caught.** No defect shipped; the cost was rounds. That's an argument the existing machinery is already adequate and I should just write better first drafts.
- **It may be my habit, not a general one.** A rule written for one agent's failure mode is how unenforced rules get in.

I think the first two are outweighed by the re-invention evidence, and the third cuts the other way — a rule that only ever helps some agents still helps them, and this one is cheap to satisfy.

## What I would *not* do

Put it in the three reviewer briefs instead. That reaches the reviewer, not the author — and the author is who writes the claim.

Also worth noting: this would go through the workflow like anything else — its own branch and commit, `code-review` binding, `ui-review` skipped with the reason stated (a rules file shows the player nothing). And per AGENTS.md's own rule, changes to the shared instruction file land on their own, not beside a feature.

Want me to do it? I'd file it as an issue first so the reasoning is on the record independently of the change, then implement — or just implement if you'd rather skip the issue for a docs-only edit.

The operative sentence is "a comment that states a number should say where the number came from", and the scoping paragraph narrows rather than widens it — "a threshold, a width, a count of rows" are all quantities. Measured against its own examples:

What was false was "the longest line that gets here", a reachability claim; `lastline` is set by `end_line()` (`tui.c:352-358`) to whatever line the game last finished.

So an author following this literally discloses the provenance of `57` and still writes the sentence that was wrong. Only the third example (the 72-column gate) is squarely a number claim. Failure scenario: the next round of exactly this defect passes the rule cleanly, which is the outcome the paragraph exists to prevent. # /proc/<pid>/status gives SigCgt, the mask of signals the process has
# handlers for, and SIGWINCH is 28 -- so bit 27. Linux only; skipped
# elsewhere, since the fix is worth having either way and the rest of
# this file already runs on macOS.
#
# The plain game is the control. Asserting only "the -t game has no
# handler" would pass on a build that never installed one for any
# reason, including one where the fallback stopped happening at all.

				n = (n * 16) + c
			}
			# bit 27, reached by halving rather than shifting:
			# POSIX awk has no >> operator.
			for (i = 0; i < 27; i++) n = int(n / 2)
			print (n % 2) ? "yes" : "no"
		}'

1. **Whether anything a player sees differs at all**, in the fallback game especially — resizing at a question and at a pause, mid-command, during the slow-printed text, and across the play-again prompt.

## 1. Verdict

**Acceptable as-is.** The claim in the task description holds under measurement: across a full fallback journey (setup questions, `srscan`, `help` paging, `chart`, `status`, quit, score-recording, play-again, second game) driven at 40x10 with fourteen resizes interleaved, the 200-line scrollback from the branch binary and from a `main` binary built in a scratch tree is **byte-identical** — the only difference anywhere is `SigCgt` bit 27. Full-screen mode is verifiably untouched: at 80x24, 72x24 and 120x40 the `-t` game still catches SIGWINCH (`SigCgt` `0x8084002`), the panels re-lay-out on resize, and `tests/tui.sh` is green. Plain mode and the piped `-t`-with-no-terminal fallback are both byte-identical to `main`. Nothing in the player-visible surface changed, and the change makes the fallback game strictly closer to what `sst.doc:1553-1559` promises. The one finding worth the author's attention is the answer to point 3, and it is not this change's fault.

## 2. Findings

### F1 — SIGTSTP: `Ctrl-Z` then `fg` leaves a fallback game unusable (should-fix, **pre-existing**, file rather than fix here)

This is the answer to your point 3, and it is worse than the `Ctrl-C` difference you saw. `Ctrl-C` is cosmetic — exit status 1 rather than 130, nothing different on screen, terminal left sane. `Ctrl-Z` is not.

Repro, from an interactive shell in a 40x10 terminal:

```
$ sst -t
Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display.
...
COMMAND> ^Z
[1]+  Stopped                 sst -t
$ fg
sst -t
<screen goes blank; nothing you type echoes; the game never answers again>
```

The player gets a black screen and a game that has to be killed from another terminal. Measured on the game's tty after `fg`: `-icrnl -icanon -echo`, and `alternate_on=1` in tmux. ncurses' TSTP handler calls `reset_prog_mode()` on resume, which switches to the alternate screen and puts the tty into curses' program mode. With `ICRNL` off the game's `fgets()` receives `\r` and never a `\n`, so it blocks forever — that is why it hangs rather than merely looking odd. `quit`+Enter after `fg` produced nothing and the process was still alive.

A plain game (`sst` with no `-t`) does the right thing: `Ctrl-Z`, `fg`, `srscan` works, tty modes `icrnl icanon echo`.

I confirmed it is **identical on `main` at 0531ec2** and on this branch, both via a real `Ctrl-Z`/`fg` under an interactive bash and via `kill -TSTP`/`-CONT`. So this branch neither causes nor worsens it. But it is the same cause the branch is fixing — `endwin()` not taking back what `initscr()` installed — and `SIGTSTP` costs a player far more than `SIGWINCH` did, since #150's `EINTR` retries mask nothing here. Suggestion: file it under step 9 citing this repro, and note in the issue that the fix is likely the same two lines widened (`sigaction` save/restore over `SIGTSTP` as well as `SIGWINCH`, on the give-up path). Do not widen this slice for it — scoping to SIGWINCH was the right call; the finding just deserves a tracked home rather than a session summary.

`SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` I would leave alone: a player sees nothing different, and the exit status only reaches a shell script.

### F2 — the comment in `sst.c` now overstates its case (nit, not player-visible)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:685-694` still says the EINTR retry matters because "once the game has fallen back to the classic display, resizing the terminal interrupts the read." After this branch it does not. Given 0531ec2 landed to make comment claims answerable, this is exactly the kind of sentence that should be brought into step — the retry is still worth having (SIGTSTP/SIGCONT reach it, per F1), but the named cause is gone. `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/osx.c:56-58` ("Same cause as `readinput()`'s") inherits the same staleness. Flagging for `code-review`; out of my scope.

### F3 — the new test's control does not control what its comment says (nit, not player-visible)

In `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh`, both arms of the loop set `want=no`, so the pair cannot discriminate: a `sigwinch_caught()` that returned `"no"` for any reason (an awk change, a different `/proc` format) passes both. The stated rationale is also not right on its own terms — "a build where the fallback stopped happening at all" would bring the panels up at 40x10, the `-t` game would then *have* the handler, and the `-t` arm alone fails. The real control is a third arm at 80x24 asserting `yes`, which is the row of your own table that this test does not check. Separately, the failure string `"...so the fallback left curses' one installed"` is printed for the plain arm too, where no fallback occurred. Again for `code-review`.

## 3. What I exercised

Built the branch with `cmake --preset debug`; built a `main` (0531ec2) binary separately from `git archive main` into a scratch tree for A/B. All tmux work on a private socket `-L uirev152 -f /dev/null`, killed on that socket only; all games run from a scratch play directory.

- **Fallback (`-t` at 40x10), branch:** fallback notice and banner read correctly; resize at the `COMMAND>` prompt with `srsc` part-typed (100x30 → 40x10 → 60x20) — the part-typed text survives and the command completes; resize x4 at `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` during `help move` — the pause is not answered; resize during the endgame `****` slow print and at "Do you want your score recorded?" with `y` part-typed; resize at "Do you want to play again?" then a second game, which stays classic and still has no SIGWINCH handler.
- **Fallback with interactive setup (`sst -t`, no args) at 40x10:** resizes between every setup question; game starts normally.
- **A/B against `main`:** identical scripted 14-resize journey on both binaries, full 200-line scrollback diffed — identical apart from `SigCgt`.
- **Full-screen:** `-t` at 80x24 (panels, `SigCgt` bit 27 set), resize to 120x40 and down to 72x24, `lrscan` after — panels re-lay-out, borders and column alignment correct at both widths.
- **Signals:** `SigCgt`/`SigIgn` read from `/proc` for `-t`-fallback, plain, and real-TUI, on both binaries; `SIGINT` to the game alone (plain exit 130, fallback exit 1, both leave the terminal sane); `Ctrl-Z`+`fg` under an interactive bash for fallback and plain, on both binaries, with `stty` and `alternate_on` read afterwards.
- **Pipes:** `tournament 7 short novice pw` scripted journey (srscan/chart/status/damages/move/quit) in plain mode and in `-t`-with-no-terminal mode, both diffed against `main` — identical.
- **Suite:** `tests/tui.sh build/debug/sst Debug` → `tui OK`.
- Consulted `sst.doc:1540-1590` (the fallback and resize promises) and `sst.c:455-495` (the fallback notice wording).

Not covered: macOS, the frozen-game path, and resize during combat damage reports (I exercised slow print only through the endgame banner).

cat > $S/i11.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

Suspend a game with `Ctrl-Z` and resume it with `fg`, and it does not
come back: the screen is blank, nothing typed echoes, and the game never
answers again. It has to be killed from another terminal.

Reproduced on `-t` at 40x10, where the game has fallen back to the
classic display. The process really is resumed — `/proc/<pid>/stat`
shows state `T` after `Ctrl-Z` and `S` after `fg` — so it is running and
not answering, rather than still stopped.

## What is not established: whether plain mode is affected too

This is the part to settle first, because two measurements disagree and
the cause follows from which is right.

- The `ui-review` sub-agent that found it reports the fallback game
  hanging and a **plain** game (`sst` with no `-t`) recovering
  correctly, with `stty` showing `-icrnl -icanon -echo` on the hung one
  and `icrnl icanon echo` on the healthy one, and `alternate_on=1` in
  tmux. On that reading the cause is ncurses' `SIGTSTP` handler, which
  `initscr()` installs and `endwin()` does not remove — `reset_prog_mode()`
  on resume puts the tty back into curses' program mode, and with
  `ICRNL` off `fgets()` never sees a newline.
- Reproducing it here under a job-control `bash -i` inside tmux, **both**
  modes hung. But that run's plain-mode arm is unreliable: the `pgrep`
  pattern used to find the process matched more than one thing, so the
  plain measurement should be discarded rather than believed.

So: the fallback hang is solid, the asymmetry is not. If plain mode also
hangs, the `SIGTSTP`-handler explanation cannot be the whole of it,
since a plain game installs no handlers at all (`SigCgt` is `0`).

Whoever picks this up should start by settling that, in a real terminal
rather than through tmux `send-keys`.

## Scope

Pre-existing. Reproduced identically on `main` at `0531ec2` and on the
branch for #152, so neither the `SIGWINCH` restore nor #150's `EINTR`
retries cause or affect it.

Related but distinct from #152: that one is about `SIGWINCH` and is
fixed. `endwin()` also leaves `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM` and `SIGTSTP`
installed — a fallback game's mask is `0x84002` where a plain game's is
`0x0` — and `SIGTSTP` is the one that would cost a player something. If
the asymmetry above holds, the fix is likely #152's two lines widened to
save and restore `SIGTSTP` on the same give-up path.

`SIGINT` is worth checking at the same time and is probably not worth
fixing: a fallback game exits 1 on `Ctrl-C` where a plain one exits 130,
which reaches a shell script and nothing a player sees.

## How to see it

In a real terminal under 72x24:

```sh
./build/debug/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw
# "Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display."
# at COMMAND>, press Ctrl-Z
fg
# type srscan and Enter -- nothing happens
stty -a        # from another terminal, against the game's tty
```

## Where it was found

By the `ui-review` sub-agent while reviewing #152, as the answer to a
question that pass was asked: whether a player is worse off for the
handlers `endwin()` leaves behind besides `SIGWINCH`. Filed rather than
folded in — #152 is scoped to `SIGWINCH`, and this needs its cause
settled before it can be fixed.

Follow the workflow in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).

Builds go through `CMakePresets.json`: `cmake --preset ci-debug`, `ctest --preset ci-debug` / `ci-release`.

## The change (issue #152)

`tui_init()` calls `initscr()` before it can know the terminal is too small for the panels; on finding it is, it calls `endwin()` and returns FALSE. `endwin()` does not take back the `SIGWINCH` handler `initscr()` installed, so a game that fell back to the classic display carried curses' handler for the whole session where a plain game has none. That asymmetry is what made every blocking read in the classic path interruptible there and nowhere else — issue #150, fixed by retrying on `EINTR`. This removes the cause.

`tui_init()` now saves the disposition before `initscr()` and restores it **on the give-up path only**. Saved and restored rather than set to `SIG_DFL`.

Files: `tui.c` (the fix), `sst.c` and `osx.c` (comments from #150 that this makes stale — they said a resize interrupts the read, which it no longer does), `tests/tui.sh` (a new case).

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sst -t` at 40x10 (fallback) | caught | **not caught** |
| `sst` plain at 40x10 | not caught | not caught |
| `sst -t` at 80x24 (real TUI) | caught | **caught** — unchanged |

**Verdict: fail** — not on the battery (every build, test and journey I ran is green, twice) but on two comment claims inside this diff that measurement contradicts. Both need a fix or an explicit resolution before commit.

## Failures

**1. `osx.c:59-61` and `sst.c:691-694` — "SIGTSTP and SIGCONT still reach this read" is contradicted by measurement. Deterministic.**

The SIGWINCH half of both comments is correct and I reproduced it. The clause added to justify keeping the `EINTR` retry is not.

Instrument: `/tmp/.../scratchpad/sigprobe.c`, a 30-line program that reproduces the fallback path exactly (`sigaction(SIGWINCH,NULL,&old); initscr(); endwin();` then optionally the restore, then `read(0,&c,1)` in the same retry shape), run under tmux at 40x10 against the same ncurses the game links (6.6.20251231).

```
mode=""        (= main)  SigCgt=0000000008084002
  kill -WINCH  -> read n=-1 errno=4(Interrupted system call)
mode=restore   (= fix)   SigCgt=0000000000084002
  kill -WINCH  -> no read return at all
  kill -TSTP then -CONT -> no read return; process state stayed S (never stopped)
  Ctrl-Z through the pty -> no read return; state stayed S
  kill -STOP then -CONT -> state T then S, still no read return (kernel restarted it)
  a real keystroke      -> read n=1 errno=0
```

- SIGCONT is not caught by the fallback game at all after the fix: `SigCgt=0x00084002` is bits 1/14/19 = SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGTSTP. Bit 17 (SIGCONT) is clear, and a genuine stop/continue cycle restarted the blocked read rather than returning `EINTR`.
- SIGTSTP is caught, but neither `kill -TSTP` nor a terminal Ctrl-Z produced a read return — ncurses' handler evidently carries `SA_RESTART`.

`see #158` does not carry the claim either: #158 records the same `0x84002` mask (which is the evidence against the SIGCONT half) and explicitly says the mechanism is unsettled. `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/AGENTS.md:237-263` is the rule this runs into — a comment stating what can and cannot reach the code should say where that came from. Keeping the retry is right; the stated reason for keeping it is what measurement rejects.

**2. `tests/tui.sh:2857-2862` — stale comment, in a file this change edits. Deterministic.**

> `tui_init()`'s giving up is what makes the difference: `initscr()` has already run and installed a SIGWINCH handler, and `endwin()` does not take it away, so the resize interrupts the read.

Present tense, and after this change it is false — the probe above shows the interruption only without the restore. This is the same staleness the diff fixes in `sst.c`, two blocks below the new case, and #157 just landed the rule about it. (The neighbouring new comment at `tests/tui.sh:2776` is fine: `endwin()` still does not take the handler back — `tui_init()` now does.)

## Answers to the five specific questions

**1. `ctest` in both presets, goldens included.** Both green, 11/11, no skips. `tui` 151.8s Debug / 142.6s Release; `golden` 43.6s / 43.4s.

**2. The Linux-only skip.** Graceful, but it does read as a pass. I simulated a system with no `/proc` (copy outside the repo, guard rewritten to `/nonexistent/proc/self/status`, run against the fixed binary): the script prints `note: no /proc, so the SIGWINCH disposition went unchecked` to stderr, prints `tui OK`, exits 0. My judgement: skipping on macOS is right (there is no `/proc` there, ever, and the fix is platform-independent while the measurement is not), but the guard should fail loudly when `${CI:-}` is set *and* `uname -s` is `Linux`. That is the case where the check is expected to run and has silently vanished (hidepid, an unusual container, a `/proc` format move), and it costs two lines. As written, on the one platform the check exists for, its disappearance is indistinguishable from success.

**3. Can the fix affect full-screen mode?** No, checked four independent ways.
- Structural: the restore sits inside the `LINES < 24 || COLS < 72` block (`tui.c:1018-1023`), which is the only early return after `initscr()`; the two earlier returns precede `initscr()`, so there is no handler to restore there. `tui_init()` has exactly one call site (`sst.c:462`) and nothing else in the tree calls `signal`/`sigaction`, so the saved disposition can never be curses' own.

- Live journey: 80x24 → resize to 100x30 → panels rebuilt at 100 columns, `status` answered → resize to 72x24 → panels rebuilt again.
- The whole `tui` suite, which is the resize-heaviest thing here, passed in both configurations.

**4. `sigwinch_caught()`'s arithmetic.** Correct for every mask this game can produce, with two quiet edges.
- Cross-checked the extracted awk against `python3 -c "(int(m,16)>>27)&1"` over nine masks including the four real ones (`0000000008084002`, `0000000000084002`, `0`, `0000000180004000`): all agree.
- Precision: `n = n*16 + c` in awk doubles loses the low bits once the mask exceeds 2^53. `ffffffffffffffff` gives `no` where the answer is `yes`. Unreachable here (nothing above signal 20 is ever caught), but it is a wrong answer rather than an error.
