1	# Super Star Trek
2	
3	Super Star Trek is an old text-only game, an early example of a turn-based space strategy sim, written in BASIC. In this game, you are the captain of the starship Enterprise, and your mission is to scout the federation space and eliminate all the invading Klingon ships. You will have to manage the ship energy carefully, use phasers and torpedoes to destroy the Klingons, and find starbases to repair damages and replenish your energy. All of this, rendered with a few characters on screen and a lot of imagination.
4	
5	Super Star Trek is probably the most famous early text-only game ever created and it inspired many other videogames. Since the code was public domain, during the years, it was changed and improved many times. There are literally thousands of versions out there. All of them are nice, but my preference goes to the classic 1978 version called Super Star Trek.
6	
7	[Read more about Star Trek and Super Star Trek.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek_%281971_video_game%29)
8	
9	### Full-screen mode
10	
11	Run `sst -t` for a full-screen interface: the short-range scan and the
12	ship's status stay on screen in two panels while the usual game
13	conversation scrolls below them. It needs a terminal of at least 72x24
14	(columns by rows) and can be combined with the fixed-coordinate option
15	(`sst -f -t`).
16	Without `-t` the game uses its classic scrolling display.
17	
18	Resizing the terminal is fine at any point. The display follows it
19	straight away — while the game is waiting for you to answer, and while
20	it is waiting for a keystroke at a pause — and both the question you
21	were asked and the answer you were halfway through typing survive, so
22	long as there is still room for them. Older text that no longer fits
23	scrolls away, as it would in any terminal.
24	
25	Dragged smaller than the 72x24 the panels ask for, they clip rather
26	than rearrange themselves. A line with more to show than there is room
27	for ends in `>`, so a shortened number is never mistaken for a small
28	one, and a heading with no room left is dropped rather than shortened.
29	A terminal too short for the panels is the panels' problem, not the
30	conversation's: they lose rows off the bottom, the grid keeping its
31	numbering for as long as it has rows to number, and the conversation
32	keeps three rows down to six — two of it and the line the prompt or the
33	pager sits on. Below six there is not that much left to divide and it
34	keeps what there is: two rows at five and one at four. So the prompt
35	stays on screen down to four rows, and down to six a paged command shows
36	a line of itself before stopping to ask — at five its one line goes to
37	the blank that `lrscan`, `chart` and `status` open with, though
38	`srscan`, which has none, still shows a line there, and at four the
39	pager takes the only row and a paged command shows nothing of itself at
40	all. Shorter than four the panels have taken the screen: the game still
41	reads what you type, with nothing on it to say so.
42	
43	Growing the terminal back brings the panels with it, however far the
44	squeeze went: they redraw from the game state, so they return full of
45	live readings. The conversation cannot be rebuilt that way — curses
46	does not reflow it — so whatever scrolled away while the window was
47	small is gone for good, and an older line that was cut short stays cut
48	short. Every reading is a command away, though, and none of them costs
49	anything: `srscan`, `status`, `chart`, `damages`.
50	
51	The line you are on usually comes back, and it is the one that matters:
52	a question or a pause the game was part way through writing is written
53	out again whole once there is room for it, so you are not left typing
54	into the tail of a prompt. A few prompts finish their line before they
55	stop to wait; those come back too, with the answer going on the row
56	below the question — or after it, where the window is down to its last
57	row.
58	Only their final line comes back, so a question asked over several
59	lines returns as the last of them. An answer you had already started
60	typing usually comes back with its question, on the row below it. You
61	may get back only one of them. Where the question ended its own line the
62	two sit on separate rows, so a wrapped answer needs three rows and a
63	window of one or two — five rows or fewer — cannot hold the pair; a
64	question that has itself wrapped needs a row more again. The question is
65	what goes, leaving your own typing with nothing above it to say what it
66	answers, and on a very wide terminal it is the answer that goes instead,
67	however tall the window is. Shorter still and only part of whichever
68	survived is left, and sometimes neither comes back, leaving older
69	conversation on screen with the game waiting behind it.
70	
71	When the question and everything you typed are both on screen, carry on
72	and answer — that is the ordinary case now. When they are not, give the
73	terminal another row or two first: that usually brings it back with
74	your typing untouched, which beats retyping it. A very wide terminal is
75	the exception — more rows will not bring the answer back there, though
76	making it narrow enough will.
77	
78	If it does not come back, or the terminal cannot grow, do not just
79	answer it, and do not press Enter either: whatever you typed is still
80	in the buffer, and a yes/no question reads the *first* letter, so an
81	`N` typed after a `y` you cannot see answers yes.
82	Press Ctrl-U first, which throws the line away, and then answer. What
83	you type lands on whatever the window happens to be showing; the line
84	it fell on clears when you press Enter, though the characters you
85	typed stay where they landed.
86	
87	If the prompt is missing or cut off and you had not started answering
88	it, press Enter. Nothing waiting behind one commits you to anything
89	then: a pause moves on, the self-destruct password reads the empty
90	answer as a refusal and stands the sequence down, and a yes/no
91	question comes back only as `Please answer with "Y" or "N":`, without
92	saying again what it asked — answer `N` there and you are back at the
93	prompt, free to give the command again.
94	
95	If full-screen mode isn't possible — the terminal is too small, the
96	game isn't attached to one (piped input, redirected output, a job with
97	no tty), or `TERM` names a terminal that can't address the cursor —
98	`-t` prints a notice and plays in the classic display instead. That
99	game stays classic to the end — enlarging the window will not bring the
100	panels up part way through it.
101	
102	A game that went classic gets the choice made again for the next one,
103	though. So if the terminal was too small and you have since made it
104	bigger, answering yes to "Do you want to play again?" starts the next
105	game with the panels. If you resized it and it is still too small, the
106	game says what size it read back rather than leaving you to wonder —
107	72x24 is the whole of what it takes, and a tmux status bar can cost you
108	the row that decides it. Leave the terminal alone and it stays quiet:
109	you were told at startup and nothing has changed since.
110	
111	If the size it names is not your window's, something has exported
112	`LINES` or `COLUMNS`. Curses believes those over the terminal, so the
113	game is measuring what they say — which is how a 100x30 window can be
114	told it is too small. Resizing moves only whichever of the two was not
115	pinned, and if that carries the measurement past 72x24 the panels come
116	up at the pinned size rather than your window's, which is worse than
117	staying classic. Unset them and start again.
118	
119	It only goes that way. Panels that are up stay up for the rest of the
120	session however you resize, as above: they clip rather than give way to
121	the classic display.

input.command:
cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
gh issue create --title "A pinned COLUMNS above the panels' minimum draws them wider than the terminal" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`tui_init()` decides whether the panels fit by testing curses' `LINES`
and `COLS` (`tui.c`, `LINES < 24 || COLS < 72`). Where `COLUMNS` is
exported, curses takes `COLS` from it rather than from the terminal, so
the gate is evaluated against a number that may describe nothing. If
that number clears 72, the panels are drawn at it — wider than the
window they are in.

Reachable on `main`, at startup, no resize involved:

```sh
cmake --preset debug && cmake --build --preset debug
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch new-session -d -x 100 -y 30 -s t \
  'env COLUMNS=190 ./build/debug/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw; sleep 30'
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch capture-pane -t t -p | head -3
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch kill-server      # your own socket, never a bare one
```

The frame runs off the pane and wraps back onto the next row:

```
lq Quadrant qqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqklq Status qqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqq
xqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqxxqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqk         x
```

The same holds for a pinned `LINES` above 24 on a shorter terminal.

## Why it matters

It is the outcome the display is otherwise careful to avoid. `sst.doc`
and `README.md` both promise that a terminal too small for the panels
gets clipping -- a `>` marker where a line has more to show -- rather
than a broken layout, and that the classic display is what you get when
the panels will not fit. Here neither happens: the panels are drawn as
though the terminal were the size somebody exported, and what the player
sees is a wrapped frame with an empty grid inside it.

`COLUMNS` is exported by plenty of ordinary environments -- Docker
images, CI runners, shell profiles -- so this is not an exotic
configuration. It only bites when the exported value disagrees with the
terminal *and* clears the minimum.

## Where it was found

By `code-review` on the #154 branch. That change makes a second route to
the same screen -- a game that went classic can retry `tui_init()`
between games, and a resize of the unpinned dimension can carry the
measurement past the floor. #154 leaves a pinned dimension alone rather
than overriding it, precisely so it does not make this worse, and its
`README.md` and `sst.doc` paragraphs now warn the player that an
exported `LINES`/`COLUMNS` is what they are fighting. But the gate
itself is untouched by that change and predates it, so it is filed here
rather than fixed there.

## Fixing it

The gate wants a size it can trust. `tui_init()` already asks the
terminal directly with `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` for its own purposes, so the
material is to hand: require the terminal's own value to clear the floor
for a dimension whose curses value came from the environment, and fall
back to the classic display when it does not.

Worth deciding at the same time what should happen when the exported
value is merely *different* rather than too small -- panels sized to 190
columns in a 100-column window are wrong whether or not 190 passes a
threshold. Related: #163, on two comments that describe this area's
resize machinery inaccurately.
EOF
)"

I have the full picture. Here is the review.

---

# Verdict: request changes

**State reviewed:** worktree at `HEAD = 91fbe91` (branch `feat/tui-retry-per-game`, no commits yet), unstaged changes to `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/{sst.c,tui.c,tui.h,tests/tui.sh,sst.doc,README.md}`. Nothing staged, nothing untracked. Summary: `tui_init()` becomes retryable per game (ioctl size query, per-variable `LINES`/`COLUMNS` respect, SIGWINCH re-install), a new "Terminal is NxM -- need 72x24, staying classic." notice on a failed retry, four new `tests/tui.sh` cases plus an `unset LINES COLUMNS`, and rewritten `README.md`/`sst.doc` paragraphs.

Nothing I found is a defect in the shipped C behavior. All of it is comment/doc accuracy and one process item — but three of those are exactly the class of claim `AGENTS.md` step 4 makes reviewable, and one is the class step 9 makes mandatory.

## What I verified positively (so you know what not to re-check)

- `pinned()` matches `_nc_getenv_num()` + the `> 0` caller test on every input I could construct: `+80`, ` 80`, `0x50`→80, `030`→24, empty, `" "`, `0`, `-1`, `80x`, `99999999999999999999`, and the 32-bit-`long` overflow edge. The comment's measured values are right.
- The claim you rewrote at `tui.c:1132-1135` is **correct**. `resized()` → `is_term_resized(builtlines, builtcols)`, which compares against `screen_lines`/`screen_columns`; with one dimension pinned those still move when the free one does, so `sync_size()` runs; with both pinned they never move, so it returns early forever. Fourth version is the right one.
- The `unset` placement is right: line 44, after `set -u`, before the first actual `tm` invocation (the earliest is inside `cleanup()` at line 95, called from `start`). It cannot mask a game defect — the only two cases that need the variables set them through `start`'s `env` prefix, independent of the ambient value.
- Your `COLUMNS=190` number checks out by construction: pinned width 190 + free height 22 → `refusedcols=190, refusedlines=22` → `Terminal is 190x22`, against the case's `80x22`. And 190 columns of panels in a 100-column pane for "regrown". Both numbers in the comment are right.
- All three width claims are exact: 57, 57, 49 columns.
- `proutf` + `skip(1)` is genuinely `prout` for a format string, and `scan()` zeroes `linecount` inside `ja()`, so the `skip(1)` cannot trip `pause(0)` there.
- `initscr()` is a no-op on the second call (`_nc_globals.init_screen` guard), so the retry leaks no `SCREEN` and the `havecursewinch` capture correctly happens once. `atexit(tui_shutdown)` can register at most once.
- The `resize_term(pinned ? LINES : ws_row, pinned ? COLS : ws_col)` expression reproduces exactly what `_nc_get_screensize()` would compute, which is why the size is stable rather than snapping back at the first repaint. That is the load-bearing property of the design and it holds.
- `gcc -std=gnu17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wmissing-prototypes -Werror -DSCORE -DCAPTURE -DCLOAKING` compiles `tui.c` and `sst.c` clean.
- The changed `sst.doc` region (1546+) is unreachable from `helpme()`: the last `Mnemonic:` topic is `SCORE` at 1294 and it terminates on the `******` at 1302. So the `sst.doc` edit is not game output. CRLF preserved throughout; `sst.c` is CRLF in all 1061 lines including the new ones.

## Findings

### Should-fix 1 — `tests/tui.sh:2791-2794`: the comment you corrected in `tui.c` is still wrong here

> `ncurses honours those over the terminal, and a dimension it has taken from the environment stops tracking the terminal -- is_term_resized() compares against the pinned size, so sync_size() returns early for the rest of the session.`

That is the third version of the sentence, the one `tui.c:1132-1135` was rewritten to fix: singular "a dimension" leading to "returns early for the rest of the session". With one dimension pinned it does not — which is precisely what the "one pinned" arm 500 lines below exists to prove. The scoping sentence four lines later ("this is the arm that holds that line for the case where both are pinned") scopes the *test*, not the mechanism claim.

Failure scenario: the next person to touch this file reads the causal sentence, concludes any pinned variable freezes `sync_size()`, and deletes the "one pinned" arm as redundant.

Fix: scope it — "with *both* pinned, `is_term_resized()` compares against a size that can never change, so `sync_size()` returns early for the rest of the session; with one, the free dimension still moves and it still runs (see `pinned()` in `tui.c`)."

### Should-fix 2 — `tests/tui.sh:2794-2796`: "panels frozen at their startup size" looks wrong, and carries no source

> `Overriding them would buy panels frozen at their startup size, whose frame breaks rather than clips on the first resize, in place of a classic display that resizes correctly.`

They would not stay frozen. `doupdate()` calls `_nc_update_screensize()` when `_sig_winch` is set, which calls `_nc_get_screensize()`, which re-reads `LINES`/`COLUMNS` — so an overriding `tui_init()` would have its ioctl size replaced by the exported one at the first repaint after any resize. In the `LINES=20 COLUMNS=70` / 100x30 case that is panels coming up at 30x100 and then *snapping to 20x70* in a 100x30 pane, not staying at 30x100. The conclusion the comment draws (don't override) is right; only the mechanism is wrong.

I derived this from the ncurses call chain rather than measuring it, which is the other half of the problem: the sentence states a mechanism and does not say where it came from, so a reviewer either trusts it or re-derives it — the thing `AGENTS.md` step 4's comment rule is about. Either measure it and say so, or state the outcome you did observe.

### Should-fix 3 — `tui.c:1136-1141`: #164 is not named beside the code that depends on it

The comment explains the trade-off ("overriding a size somebody set on purpose would buy panels that never follow the terminal again") without naming the issue that trade-off leaves open. And this change does depend on the unfixed behavior in a way that is more than incidental: the retry can now bring panels up sized to a pinned dimension that does not match the window — reachable, e.g., `LINES=30` in a 60x20 pane, widened to 100x20, retry succeeds at 30x100, prompt off the bottom of a 20-row pane — and `README.md`/`sst.doc` now carry a paragraph warning players about exactly that shape. `AGENTS.md` step 9: "Where the work depends on the unfixed behavior, name the issue in a comment beside it. Write that comment as part of the implementation, so it reaches the reviewer rather than arriving after approval."

Fix: add `#164` to that paragraph. (Same argument applies, more weakly, to `#162` at `sst.c:566` — the `skip(1)` comment describes the `proutf` behavior without the issue number. Worth one token; I would not block on it.)

### Should-fix 4 — `README.md:116` / `sst.doc:1568`: "which is worse than staying classic" is not true for the pinned-*smaller* case

The paragraph is correctly gated ("If the size it names is not your window's"), and for the pinned-larger case it is right. But the pinned-smaller case reaches the same paragraph and gets the wrong advice: `COLUMNS=80` exported in a 200-column window, `LINES` free at 20 → refused, notice reads `Terminal is 80x20` (not the window's 200), player grows height to 30 → retry succeeds → panels at 30x80 inside a 200x30 window. That is a working full-screen display using 80 of 200 columns, not something "worse than staying classic" — and the doc has just told that player to unset `COLUMNS` and start again.

This matters more than usual because the same paragraph's `pinned()` counterpart in `tui.c:1015-1017` argues the opposite way about the same variable: "COLUMNS alone is exported by plenty of Docker images, CI runners and shell profiles … and it is usually the right width."

feat(tui): make the full-screen choice again for each game

tui_init() ran once, before the play-again loop, so a player who
started on a terminal too small for the panels, grew it, finished the
game and answered yes got another classic game -- on a terminal that
would now hold the panels, with nothing on screen to say so. It is now
retried once per game, at the foot of that loop. Not per resize:
mid-game is the one time there is a game on screen to lose.

Three things inside tui_init() had to change for a second call to work,
each measured against ncurses 6.6.20251231.

A second initscr() reports the stale size -- 70x20 grown to 100x30
still reads 20x70, is_term_resized() agrees nothing changed, and
resize_term(0, 0) leaves it there -- so the retry refused itself. It
now asks the terminal with ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ).

ncurses installs its SIGWINCH handler once per process, so after #152's
give-up path restored the old disposition a second initscr() got none:
a resize under getch() then produced no KEY_RESIZE and no keypress, and
the read simply stayed blocked. Curses' own handler is captured at the
first initscr() and re-installed.

Neither override touches a dimension the environment has pinned.
ncurses honours LINES and COLUMNS over the terminal and then stops
following it on that axis, so overriding bought panels that could never
follow the window again -- worse than the classic display they
replaced. pinned() mirrors ncurses' own rule from _nc_getenv_num, base
0 and fitting an int, and is asked per variable because ncurses honours
them per variable: taking either to pin both stood the whole retry down
for anyone with COLUMNS exported.

The refusal size is recorded so the retry can tell a player who resized
and missed -- 80x22, or "80x24" inside tmux where the status bar leaves
23 rows -- from one who changed nothing. The first is told what was
measured, not only what is wanted; the second gets silence.

The startup notice's second line said the session was stuck classic,
which is no longer true, and sst.doc and README.md described the same
limitation. All three now describe the decision instead, and both
manuals gained a paragraph on exported LINES/COLUMNS, which is how a
100x30 window comes to be told it is too small.

tests/tui.sh gains five cases -- the panels coming back and following a
later resize, the measured-size notice, the silence, an exported size
keeping the last word, and one pinned dimension not standing the retry
down -- and unsets LINES and COLUMNS, which tmux otherwise hands to the
game from whoever runs the suite.

Plain mode is byte-identical over a deterministic two-game journey.

ui-review ran four rounds, verifier six, code-review six.

Closes #154

Closes #154.

## The slice

`tui_init()` ran once, before the play-again loop, so a player who
started on a terminal too small for the panels, grew it, finished the
game and answered yes got **another classic game** — on a terminal that
would now hold the panels, with nothing on screen to say so. It is now
retried once per game, at the foot of that loop. Deliberately not per
resize: mid-game is the one time there is a game on screen to lose.

## What a player sees

| situation | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| grew the terminal past 72x24, played again | classic, silently | **panels** |
| grew it and missed (80x22) | classic, silently | `Terminal is 80x22 -- need 72x24, staying classic.` |
| changed nothing | classic, silently | classic, silently |

The startup notice's second line was `It stays classic: restart sst at
72x24 to get the panels.` — no longer true. It is now `Grow the terminal
to 72x24 and the next game gets panels.` Both are 57 columns, measured.

## Three things `tui_init()` needed before a second call worked

Each measured against ncurses 6.6.20251231:

1. **A second `initscr()` reports the stale size.** 70x20 grown to
   100x30 still reads 20x70; `is_term_resized()` agrees nothing changed
   and `resize_term(0, 0)` leaves it there. The retry refused itself.
   Fixed with `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)`.
2. **ncurses installs its SIGWINCH handler once per process,** so after
   #152's give-up path restored the old disposition a second `initscr()`
   got none — a resize under `getch()` produced no `KEY_RESIZE` *and no
   keypress*, so the read stayed blocked. Curses' own handler is
   captured at the first `initscr()` and re-installed.
3. **Neither override touches a pinned dimension.** ncurses honours
   `LINES`/`COLUMNS` over the terminal and then stops following it on
   that axis, so overriding bought panels that could never follow the
   window again. `pinned()` mirrors `_nc_getenv_num` — base 0, above
   zero, fits an int — and is asked **per variable**, because ncurses
   honours them per variable.

Point 3 took three attempts and every one was caught by review; see
below.

## Review found four real defects in this change

This is the part worth reading.

- **The ioctl override froze the panels.** Bringing them up under an
  exported `LINES`/`COLUMNS` looked like an improvement — it fixed a
  corrupted grid — but ncurses then stops tracking the terminal, so
  `sync_size()` returns early forever: panels frozen at their startup
  size, the frame breaking rather than clipping. `verifier` had
  confirmed the override as an improvement one round earlier; nobody had
  looked at what happened *afterwards*. Found by `code-review`.
- **The first fix printed a false notice every game.** With the size
  pinned, `tui_size_changed_since_refusal()` read the terminal while the
  recorded refusal came from curses — two sources that can never agree —
  so a player who touched nothing was told the terminal had moved, with
  a size that was not their window. Found by `code-review` and
  `verifier` independently, from opposite ends.
- **The second fix killed the feature for anyone with `COLUMNS` set.**
  Treating either variable as pinning both is wrong: ncurses pins them
  independently, and `COLUMNS` alone — Docker images, CI runners, shell
  profiles — is usually the *right* width, with only the height ever
  wrong. Found by both passes.
- **`proutf` does not end its line.** Switching from `prout` to
  interpolate the measured size ran the notice into the next question.
  Caught by my own test, sideways — it failed on the *wrapped question*,
  not the notice. Now #162.

## Behaviour beyond #154, disclosed

Under an exported `LINES`/`COLUMNS` the game behaves exactly as `main`
does, including `main`'s pre-existing corrupted grid. An earlier state
of this branch changed that; it was reverted for the reason above.

## Testing

`tests/tui.sh` gains five cases: the panels coming back and **following
a later resize**, the measured-size notice, the silence, an exported
size keeping the last word, and one pinned dimension not standing the
retry down. It also `unset`s `LINES`/`COLUMNS` — tmux hands the client
environment to the pane, so an exported `COLUMNS=190` made the suite
assert `80x22` against a game printing `190x22`. `verifier` proved that
line load-bearing: deleting it fails **78 checks** under a polluted
environment.

Six mutation proofs, each on a copy outside the repository, each
recorded beside the assertion it proved:

| break | fails |
| --- | --- |
| SIGWINCH re-install deleted | the resize-follow check alone |
| ioctl deleted | the two panels-came-back checks |
| ioctl skipped on the first call only | the `env size:` check alone |
| `resized` test dropped | the unchanged-terminal check alone |
| `getenv` pair deleted | the `env size:` check alone |
| guard on the first call only (the narrower fix proposed in review) | the retry check alone — **it passes every other check in the file** |

That last one is why the fix went further than proposed.

Plain mode is byte-identical to `main` over a deterministic two-game
journey. `ctest` 11/11 in both `ci-*` presets.

## Resolved explicitly rather than fixed

- **The base-0 and int-bound halves of `pinned()` have no test.** They
  diverge only for `LINES=0x50`, `LINES=030` and overflow values, which
  no real environment exports; each case costs a tmux session in a file
  already near three minutes. Both are measured in the comment beside
  `pinned()`, by me.
- **The restored screen after a successful retry** shows the first
  game's transcript, so `play again?y` sits above the farewell. The only
  honest cushion would print before the outcome is known. `ui-review`
  agreed and could not find one either.
- **The 72x24 boundary on retry, and silence on a non-size refusal,**
  have no automated case; `verifier` exercised both by hand and the
  boundary is the same gate the startup cases already cover.

## Filed, not fixed

- **#162** — `proutf()` is named like `prout()` but behaves like
  `proutn()`. It caused the defect above, and it is why the end-of-game
  questions share a line in shipped output.
- **#163** — two pre-existing `tui.c` comments describe
  `resize_term(0, 0)` and `is_term_resized()` as doing things they do
  not. The second is the mechanism behind the frozen-panels defect: the
  trap looked safe *because* of that comment.
- **#164** — a pinned `COLUMNS` above 72 clears the gate's column half
  whatever the window is, so the panels are drawn wider than the
  terminal and the frame wraps back onto the row below. Reachable on
  `main` at startup with no resize. Named in a comment beside the code
  that depends on it.

## Passes

`ui-review` ×4 (final: acceptable as-is), `verifier` ×6 (final: PASS,
11/11 in both `ci-*`), `code-review` ×6 (final: **approve**).

The approval was given on the state before three comment and
documentation corrections that the same review prescribed as
non-blocking — it said explicitly that fixing them changes nothing
compiled or player-visible. I applied them, and measured the one claim
they rested on rather than inheriting it: with `COLUMNS=100` pinned in
an 80-column pane the status panel's border does wrap back onto the
quadrant's coordinate row, so the docs say that rather than "off the
edge", which would have read as the tidy clipping the README promises
elsewhere.

All four CI jobs pass on both platforms, merge state CLEAN. **[PR #165](https://github.com/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/pull/165)** is ready.

**What shipped** — `tui_init()` is retried once per game at the foot of the play-again loop. Grow a too-small terminal, finish the game, answer yes, and the next one comes up full-screen. Grow it and miss (80x22, or "80x24" in tmux where the status bar takes a row) and the game tells you the size it actually measured. Change nothing and it stays quiet.

Three things had to change inside `tui_init()` for a second call to work at all, each measured against ncurses 6.6.20251231: a second `initscr()` reports the *stale* size; ncurses installs its SIGWINCH handler once per process, so the retry got none and a resize left the read blocked with no `KEY_RESIZE` and no keypress; and neither override may touch a dimension the environment pinned.

**Review found four real defects, and the last one is the reason this took ten rounds.** My ioctl override brought the panels up under an exported `LINES`/`COLUMNS` — which looked like an improvement, since it fixed a corrupted grid, and `verifier` had confirmed it as one. But ncurses then stops tracking the terminal, so the panels froze at their startup size and the frame broke instead of clipping. The first fix printed a false notice every game; the second killed the feature for anyone with `COLUMNS` exported, which Docker images and CI runners routinely do. Only the third — per-variable, using ncurses' own parse rule — is right.

The evidence that going further than proposed was necessary: the narrower fix suggested in review **passes every other check in the file**, and fails only the arm added to catch it.

Six mutation proofs, each on a copy outside the repo, each recorded beside its assertion. `verifier` separately proved the new `unset LINES COLUMNS` is load-bearing — deleting it fails 78 checks under a polluted environment, because tmux hands the caller's environment straight to the game.

**Filed, not fixed: #162, #163, #164.** #163 is the pointed one — two pre-existing comments describe `resize_term(0, 0)` and `is_term_resized()` as doing things they don't, and the second is precisely why the frozen-panels trap looked safe.

One disclosure: `code-review` approved the state before three comment and doc corrections it had itself prescribed as non-blocking. I applied them and measured the claim they rested on rather than inheriting it — with `COLUMNS=100` pinned in an 80-column pane, the status panel's border really does wrap onto the quadrant's coordinate row, so the docs say that rather than "off the edge", which would have read as the tidy clipping the README promises elsewhere.

Merged. `#154` is closed, branch deleted, `main` clean at `c98a422`.

**Two issues closed this session** — `#153` (the `.gitignore` slice) and `#154` (the per-game full-screen retry). Four filed along the way, all still open:

- **#160** — `sst.doc` promises `freeze` always makes a `.TRK` file; three things about the name are undocumented (the dot rule, the nine-character truncation, and that it must start with a letter).
- **#162** — `proutf()` is named like `prout()` but behaves like `proutn()`. It caused a real defect in #154 and explains the run-together end-of-game questions in shipped output.
- **#163** — two `tui.c` comments describe `resize_term(0,0)` and `is_term_resized()` as doing things they don't. This is the one I'd fix first: the second comment is *why* the frozen-panels trap in #154 looked safe, so it's actively misleading the next person to touch the resize path.
- **#164** — a pinned `COLUMNS` above 72 clears the gate's column half whatever the window is, so the panels draw wider than the terminal and the frame wraps. Reachable on `main` at startup.

The through-line worth noting: both slices spent nearly all their review rounds on *claims*, not code. The `.gitignore` rule was byte-identical from the first draft through six rounds while six false statements were found in its comment — every one asserting an outcome rather than a mechanism. #154 repeated it at a larger scale, where a comment I'd written in #152 correctly predicted the SIGWINCH problem, and a comment I *hadn't* written correctly — the one #163 covers — is what made a real defect look safe. Review the user-facing behaviour of the change on branch `fix/tui-resize-comments` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek. Read AGENTS.md and .claude/agents/ui-review.md.

content.text:
## 1. Verdict

**Acceptable as-is on player-visible behaviour.** The deleted `resize_term(0, 0)` was provably inert on this curses: a standalone probe shows `resize_term(0,0)` returns `ERR` on ncurses 6.6.20251231 (non-positive dimensions are rejected before any work is done), and every paired capture I took — ~55 screens across two binaries built from the same tree differing only in that line — is byte-identical. I dragged terminals in every state the brief names (pending question, pause waiting on a keystroke, mid-command slow-print, during setup, part way through a `help` topic, mid-combat, below 72x24, down to 4 rows, width-only and height-only, and rapid repeated drags) and found no difference from `main`, and nothing that reads wrong on its own terms. The "between reads" case the rewritten comment rests on **is real and I reproduced it** — a drag during the self-destruct countdown was acted on by `sync_size()` at the next repaint (`built=80x24` vs `LINES/COLS=100x30`) — so the comment's core justification stands. Two findings are about the comments' *cited evidence*, both in the file the change exists to make honest.

## 2. Findings

### should-fix — the measurement quoted in `resized()`'s comment cannot show what it is quoted for
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:315-317`:

```
 * Measured against ncurses 6.6.20251231: with the pane grown from
 * 100x30 to 120x40 and no curses call made in between,
 * is_term_resized(LINES, COLS) still answered 0. #163.
```

`is_term_resized(LINES, COLS)` compares `LINES`/`COLS` against the same cached screen size those globals are read from, so it is 0 **by construction**, whether or not curses has processed the resize. My probe (curses program, pane grown 100x30 → 120x40 during a `sleep`, no curses call in between):

```
before any curses call:  LINES=30 COLS=100  is_term_resized(LINES,COLS)=0  is_term_resized(30,100)=0
after doupdate():        LINES=40 COLS=120  is_term_resized(LINES,COLS)=0  is_term_resized(30,100)=1
```

The conclusion the comment draws is correct — the second column proves it — but the sentence offered as proof would print `0` on a terminal that had never moved, and `0` again after curses had fully adopted the new size. Under AGENTS.md's "a claim carrying its source is one the next reader checks in a minute", this one fails the check it invites, in the one comment whose subject is a claim that failed exactly that way. Suggested replacement, using the call `resized()` actually makes: *"with the pane grown from 100x30 to 120x40 and no curses call made in between, `is_term_resized(30, 100)` — the built size, which is what this asks — still answered 0; the first `doupdate()` moved LINES/COLS to 40/120 and the same call then answered 1."*

### nit — "seen by nobody until the next repaint asks" invites the misreading #163 exists to remove
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:911-916`. Instrumented run (copy outside the repository; log around `wgetch` and at `sync_size` entry), dragging 80x24 → 100x30 during the destruct countdown, i.e. strictly between reads:

```
--- marker: drag now (between reads, mid-countdown) ---
sync_size: built=80x24 LINES/COLS=100x30 resized=1
getch wgetch -> 410 KEY_RESIZE (LINES/COLS=100x30 built=100x30)
```

So the repaint does act first — but the reader **also** gets a `KEY_RESIZE` for that same drag. "The report reaches only a reader … is seen by nobody until the next repaint asks" reads as "that drag produces no report at all", which is the same shape as the sentence being replaced ("gives curses nothing to hand back"), and the next person who instruments `wgetch` — as this change's author did — will see 410 arrive and conclude the new comment is wrong too. What the placement actually buys is ordering: `tui_readline`/`tui_getch` repaint *before* `wgetch` can report, so without `sync_size()` there the first frame of the next prompt is drawn to the old geometry. Worth noting the converse as well, since it bounds the claim: where no curses call happens between the drag and the repaint, `resized()` answers 0 at that repaint (first probe above) and it is `KEY_RESIZE` that fixes it a moment later. Suggested shape: say that the repaint is what notices *first*, that the reader's `KEY_RESIZE` still follows, and that the frame drawn before it is the thing this prevents.

### nit (no action expected) — portability of the deleted call
`resize_term(0, 0)` is a documented idiom in *PDCurses* ("adjust to the actual window size"), not in ncurses, where non-positive arguments are rejected. This project builds against ncurses (verified `ERR` here), so the removal is a no-op; I mention it only so the next reader does not re-add it after seeing that idiom elsewhere. Nothing to change.

### Verified as accurate
`sync_size()`'s new "curses has already taken the new size itself; measured in a running game, `sync_size()` found LINES and COLS at 120x40 against windows built at 100x30" — independently reproduced in my instrumented run (`built=80x24 LINES/COLS=100x30`), and `doupdate()` alone moved `LINES` 30 → 40 in the standalone probe with no `resize_term` call by the application.

## 3. What I exercised

Two binaries: the working tree (`build/debug/sst`) and a scratch copy of the same tree with `git show HEAD:tui.c` restored, built with the same `debug` preset. Determinism via `tournament` seeds (42, 22). All tmux work on a private socket (`-L uirev -f /dev/null`), killed at the end; repo left with only the reviewed `tui.c` modification and no stray files.

- **A — setup question pending:** 80x24 → 100x30 → 72x24 → 60x20 (clipping) → 80x24, then `tournament 42 / short / novice / password`, in-game grow to 120x40, `srscan`, shrink 74x26, `lrscan`, `chart`. 12/12 captures identical.
- **B — pause waiting on a keystroke:** briefing `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` dragged to 100x32 / 72x24 / 66x18 / back; then `help move` paged, dragged at page 1 and page 2 (90x20), to end of topic. 13/13 identical.
- **C — between reads (the case the new comment rests on):** `destruct`, dragged mid slow-print countdown (grow 100x30, then shrink 74x22), password prompt, second countdown dragged to 96x28, endgame. Run twice per binary to separate timing jitter from real difference: 5/5 identical within and across binaries. Confirms panels stay at the old geometry during the countdown and rebuild at the next prompt, identically in both builds.
- **D — part-typed answer + extremes:** `move manu` typed but unsent, then 120x30, 74x30 (width-only), 74x24 (height-only), 72x24, 40x10, 34x6, 30x4, back to 80x24, then completing the command. 10/10 identical; the partial answer survives at every size including 4 rows.
- **E — setup-time drag, rapid drags, endgame:** drag 50 ms after the password answer while the briefing prints; six drags in ~0.5 s while blocked at `COMMAND>`; `quit`, score prompt, play-again at 60x16, next game. 9/9 identical.
- **F — refusal and retry:** started at 70x20 (classic display), grown to 100x30 mid-game, played, `play again` retry, 76x24, second game grown. Identical apart from time-seeded randomness in the `regular` game.
- **G — damaged sensors:** `debug` → selective damage → `srscan` masked, at 100x30 / 72x24 / 40x12 / 80x24, checking the `SENSORS DAMAGED` caption on the bottom border. 6/6 identical.
- **H — combat:** tournament 22 / long / good (starts Condition RED), `phasers 400` with a drag mid-exchange down to 72x24, `[CONTINUE?]` pause, `shields up`, `damages`, `chart` at 72x24 and 100x30. 10/10 identical.
- **Plain mode:** scripted `tournament 42` journey (srscan/lrscan/chart/status/damages/report/move/quit) byte-identical between the two binaries; `sync_size()` is unreachable without `-t`.
- **Curses-level probes:** standalone programs for `resize_term(0,0)`'s return value and for `is_term_resized` semantics before/after `doupdate()`; instrumented game copy (outside the repository) logging `sync_size` and every `wgetch` return.

I did not run `ctest`, `tests/tui.sh`, or the golden battery — that is the verifier's scope, and the brief reports `tui.sh` already green.

getch wgetch -> 410 KEY_RESIZE (LINES/COLS=100x30 built=100x30)
```

Suggested shape: say that the repaint is what notices *first*, that the reader's `KEY_RESIZE` still follows, and that the frame drawn before it is the thing this prevents.

`resize_term(0, 0)` is a documented idiom in *PDCurses* ("adjust to the actual window size"), not in ncurses, where non-positive arguments are rejected. This project builds against ncurses (verified `ERR` here), so the removal is a no-op; I mention it only so the next reader does not re-add it after seeing that idiom elsewhere. Nothing to change.

## Failures

None. No check failed, and nothing looked flaky. The only red output I produced came from three bugs in my own throwaway journey driver (sent `y` to "play again?" when I meant `n`; missed the pager between the destruct prompt lines; asserted the post-drag repaint 3 s in, while `prouts` was still printing the countdown). All three were driver errors, corrected, and the corrected runs pass deterministically — 3 runs of the destruct journey (2x ci-debug, 1x ci-release), 3 runs of the resize journey (80x24 debug, 72x24 debug, 80x24 release).

## The removal: `resize_term(0, 0)`

You asked for a third angle rather than a repeat. I took it at the library boundary, not at the screen, and it is stronger than either of the first two: the call is inert **by construction**, not just in the states that were reached.

`objdump -d --disassemble=resize_term_sp /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libncurses.so.6` — the first instructions of the function, before anything else:

```
1cc14: test %esi,%esi        # ToLines <= 0 ?
1cc16: setle %al
1cc19: test %edx,%edx        # ToCols  <= 0 ?
1cc1b: setle %cl
1cc1e: or   %ecx,%eax
1cc20: test %rdi,%rdi        # SP == 0 ?
1cc23: sete %cl
1cc26: or   %cl,%al
1cc28: jne  1ce83
...
1ce83: mov  $0xffffffff,%eax # ERR
1ce88: ret
```

`resize_term()` itself is a two-instruction thunk into `resize_term_sp`. So with a zero argument the function returns `-1` from its entry test and touches no screen state, whatever the game was doing — there is no path, reached or unreached, on which it could have done anything. A probe confirms the same from the outside: `rt(0,0)=ERR`, `rt(0,COLS)=ERR`, `rt(LINES,0)=ERR`, `rt(-1,-1)=ERR`, all with `LINES`/`COLS` unmoved, while `rt(LINES,COLS)=OK` and `rt(30,100)=OK` move them — the ERR is the argument, exactly as your comment says ("ncurses wanting a positive size"), and not the game's state.

Scope note, honestly: this is ncurses 6.6.20251231, which is both the installed version and the one your comments cite. I did not test any other version, so "inert" is verified for this library only — and deleting the call is what removes the dependence on which version is underneath.

I reproduced your measurement independently (own probe, own tmux socket, pane grown 100x30 → 120x40, windows "built" at the old size), and every line of it matches:

```

after initscr            LINES= 30 COLS=100 itr(built)=0 itr(LINES,COLS)=0
  before any curses call LINES= 30 COLS=100 itr(built)=0 itr(LINES,COLS)=0   <- pane already 120x40
  after doupdate         LINES= 40 COLS=120 itr(built)=1 itr(LINES,COLS)=0
```

- **"compares against the screen size curses has cached, which is what LINES and COLS report"** — confirmed. `is_term_resized(built)` flips 0 → 1 at exactly the moment `LINES`/`COLS` move, and not when the terminal moved.
- **"answerable only once curses has processed the resize"** — confirmed. Six ticks over three seconds with the pane already at 120x40 and the answer still 0; `doupdate()` is what changes it.
- **"is_term_resized(LINES, COLS) … is 0 whatever the terminal has done"** — confirmed in all 26 snapshots, including the ones taken while the terminal was 120x40 and the cache 100x30. This is the claim you wanted checked twice; it is right, and it is right for the reason given.
- **"ncurses 6.6.20251231"** — `pkg-config --modversion ncurses` says exactly that.
- **"used to call resize_term(0, 0) to do it"** — the deleted comment in `890267f` (#47) read `/* adopt whatever the terminal is now */`; that commit introduced both the call and the wording, and the line has not changed since.

The closing paragraph of `sync_size()`'s comment in `tui.c` says:

```
 * The message window's contents are lost -- curses cannot reflow them
 * and the game keeps no transcript -- so the panels come back and the
 * conversation carries on from wherever it had got to.
```

A grow keeps them. `make_windows()` uses `wresize()`, which preserves
what is already in the window. Measured, `sst -t tournament 7 short
novice pw` at 90x30:

```
COMMAND> status          <- run status, six lines of readings printed

  Stardate      4800.0
  Condition     GREEN
  Position      3 - 2, 7 - 9

The whole conversation is still there afterwards.

and cannot come back when the terminal grows again, because curses has
nothing left to reflow from and the game keeps no transcript. That is
what `README.md` describes correctly -- "whatever scrolled away while
the window was small is gone for good, and an older line that was cut

precisely because everything else is unrecoverable once clipped.

the file, and it says the display throws away more than it does. A
maintainer reading it would think a grow costs the player their
conversation -- and might add machinery to preserve something curses is
already preserving, or delete `restore_curline()`'s careful handling on
the grounds that everything is lost anyway.

comments in the same area. Filed rather than fixed there: #163 is about
how a resize is *detected* -- `is_term_resized()`, `resize_term(0, 0)`,

do not come back; a grow keeps what is there. Worth checking the same

from wherever it had got to" is true, but it reads as a consolation for
a loss that did not happen.

the same resize behaviour.

fix(tui): say what the resize path actually does

Seven comments around sync_size() described machinery that does not
exist, all of them from #47, and one line of code did nothing at all.

resize_term(0, 0) never adopted anything. Logged in a running game it
returned ERR on every call, with LINES and COLS identical either side
and already holding the new size before it ran -- curses had adopted
the resize itself. The verifier took the same question to the library
and disassembled resize_term_sp: the non-positive argument test is the
first thing in the function, so the call was inert by construction and
not merely in the states anyone reached. Deleted, which is the whole of
the compiled change.

is_term_resized() does not ask the terminal, whatever resized()'s
comment said. It compares against the screen size curses has cached,
which is what LINES and COLS report, so it can answer only once curses
has processed the resize: with the pane grown 100x30 to 120x40 and no
curses call in between it still said no, and the first doupdate() moved
LINES and COLS and it said yes.

A drag during a blocked read does give curses something to hand back.
Instrumenting tui_readline() shows KEY_RESIZE delivered for exactly the
case the comment said produced nothing. What calling sync_size() before
every repaint really buys is the drag that lands while no reader waits
-- a destruct countdown, a quadrant being set up -- and that needs some
curses call since the drag, which the countdown supplies by refreshing
after every character.

builtlines and builtcols were said to be there so an empty read could
be told from an interrupted one. That reader went at #79 and took the
question with it; sync_size() is now resized()'s only caller.

make_windows() was said to delete what was there first. There is no
delwin in the file, and the branch fifty lines below says the opposite
and explains why -- keeping the window is the reason the mvwin() beside
it is needed at all.

The message window's contents were said to be lost. A grow keeps them:
wresize() preserves, and a whole status readout survived 90x30 becoming
110x36. A shrink is what costs, permanently, which is why
restore_curline() goes to the trouble it does.

No behaviour changes. ui-review built a second binary with the deleted
line restored and found ~55 paired screens byte-identical across every
state it could reach.

Closes #163
Closes #166

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Review the user-facing behaviour of the change on branch `fix/tui-gate-pinned-size` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek. Read AGENTS.md and .claude/agents/ui-review.md.

**State:** no commits (HEAD `be20d61` = `main`); unstaged in `sst.c`, `tui.c`, `tui.h`, `tests/tui.sh`, `sst.doc`, `README.md`.

## What it does

Issue **#164**. `tui_init()`'s gate is `LINES < 24 || COLS < 72`, asked of curses — and where the environment has pinned `LINES` or `COLUMNS`, curses' number need not be the window's. A pinned size that clears the floor was drawn whatever the terminal actually was, so the display did not fit the screen it was on.

I reproduced both axes on `main` before changing anything:

- `COLUMNS=190` in a 100-column pane: the frame runs off the edge and wraps back over the quadrant panel's coordinate row (`xqqqqq1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 10qqxx…`).
- `LINES=40` in a 20-row pane: the panels draw fine — they cap at `PANELH` — but the message window's lower rows are off the bottom, so the conversation walks off screen. After six `status` commands the last visible row read ` COMMAND> t     7.00`: a prompt on top of half a status line.

Neither is the clipping the manual promises for a small terminal.

**Now the game refuses and plays classic**, with a notice of its own:

```
Terminal is 100x30 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 190x30.
Unset them and start again to get the panels.
```

52 columns and 45 at three-digit sizes, both measured, inside the 57 the other notices hold. It is deliberately different advice from the too-small pair, which says to grow the window: growing does not help here, and neither does answering yes at "play again", because nothing in a session can unset an exported variable.

**A pinned dimension smaller than the window is deliberately left alone** — the panels are then drawn narrow or short with room to spare, which works, and refusing it would take the display from anyone whose profile exports a `COLUMNS` that happens to be right. Verified: `COLUMNS=80` in a 140x36 pane still brings the panels up at 80.

## What I checked myself

- Full `tests/tui.sh` → `tui OK`, including the two new `fallback` cases and the `env size:` and `one pinned:` cases from #165.
- Plain mode byte-identical over a deterministic two-game journey, 81 lines.
- 80x24 and 72x24 draw normally — the new gate cannot fire when nothing is pinned, since curses' size is then the terminal's.

## What I want from you

- **The new notice, as a player reads it.** Is "LINES/COLUMNS make it 190x30" intelligible to someone who does not know what those are? The second line tells them what to do; the first is trying to explain why. Compare it against the three notices already there.
- **Whether refusing is the right answer at all**, versus drawing something clipped. My argument is that the classic display fits any window and a wrapped frame does not, but you are the one who judges what a player would rather have.
- **The boundary**: a pinned size exactly equal to the window, and one a single row or column over. The gate is `LINES > ws_row || COLS > ws_col`.
- **The `LINES=40` case specifically** — the panels looked fine there at first glance and only went wrong as the conversation grew, so a player might reasonably think it was working. Does refusing at startup feel right, or does it take away a display that looked usable?
- Anything the earlier rounds on this machinery did not reach.

Same constraints: private tmux socket via `-L <yourname>` with `-f /dev/null`, never a bare `kill-server`, never `kill-session` on a session you did not create, scratch directory with a copy of `sst.doc`, never redirect the game's stdout in the pane.

Read-only: report findings, never edit.

content.text:
## Verdict

The core decision is right and the new startup notice reads well: I reproduced both failure modes on `main` (at `COLUMNS=190`/100-col pane the frame runs off the edge; at `LINES=40`/20-row pane the conversation walks off the bottom until the last visible row was literally ` COMMAND> t     7.00`), and the branch replaces both with a classic display that fits the window, a two-line notice inside the 57-column budget the other notices hold, and an exact boundary that behaves as documented (pinned == window draws panels, +1 refuses, pinned smaller still draws). **It needs changes before commit**, though, for one thing the change introduces and does not cover: the *between-games* retry notice now quotes the pinned size and contradicts itself — a player who does exactly what the too-small notice asked is told `Terminal is 190x30 -- need 72x24, staying classic.` The documentation also asserts something the retry path does not do, and states the old "the panels come up at the pinned size" claim two sentences before retracting it.

## Findings

### 1. should-fix (I considered blocker) — the play-again retry notice now tells the player a size their window does not have, and a requirement they already exceed
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:571-583` (the `tui_refused_size()` branch) is unchanged, but this branch makes it newly reachable with an *oversize* refusal behind it, so `refusedcols`/`refusedlines` now carry curses' inflated number.

Reproduced, two ways, both starting from a notice the game itself printed:

- Pane 100x20, `COLUMNS=190`. Startup: `Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display.` / `Grow the terminal to 72x24 and the next game gets panels.` Player grows the pane to 100x30 — exactly what was asked — answers `y`, and gets:
  `Terminal is 190x30 -- need 72x24, staying classic.`
- Pane 100x20, `LINES=40`. Startup: the new notice. Player widens to 120x20, answers `y`:
  `Terminal is 120x40 -- need 72x24, staying classic.` (their window is 120x**20**.)

What a player experiences: a size that is not their terminal's, a stated requirement of 72x24 that the quoted size plainly clears, and no mention of `LINES`/`COLUMNS` at all — so no way forward. On `main` this string could never carry a pinned oversize number (the oversize case brought the panels up instead), so it is this change that opens the path. It also falsifies the new doc sentence "the game says both sizes and plays classic instead", which is true only of the startup path.

Suggestion: ask `tui_refused_oversize()` in the retry branch too and print the pinned-size wording there (the same two lines, or a one-line form such as `Terminal is 120x20 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 120x40.`), falling through to `Terminal is %dx%d -- need 72x24, staying classic.` only for a genuinely too-small window. The startup path already has exactly the right sentence; the retry path just needs to reach it.

### 2. should-fix — the manual states the superseded behavior, then retracts it two sentences later
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/README.md:110-120` and `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.doc:1563-1571` still say "...if that carries the measurement past 72x24 the panels come up at the pinned size rather than your window's", and then "Pinned larger they would not fit the screen at all, so the game says both sizes and plays classic instead." A reader takes the first claim, then has to unlearn it. Suggestion: make the middle sentence conditional — e.g. "...and if that carries the measurement past 72x24 the game looks at whether the pinned size fits your window" — so the pinned-smaller and pinned-larger sentences that follow each complete it rather than one contradicting it.

### 3. should-fix (small) — the new notice is the only fallback that does not say what display you are getting
The three existing notices all name the outcome: "using the classic display" (twice) and "staying classic". The new pair says what is wrong and what to do, and then the game simply starts classic:

```
Terminal is 100x30 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 190x30.
Unset them and start again to get the panels.
```

A player can infer it from "to get the panels", but the established shape here is outcome line + action line, and this one is diagnosis + action. Suggestion, both within budget: keep line 1 and make line 2 `Using the classic display; unset them and start again.` (54 columns), or keep line 2 as-is and end line 1 with the outcome if you can spare the width. Either keeps the deliberate "start again", not "resize", advice you were after.

### 4. nit — "LINES/COLUMNS ... them" when only one is pinned, and the offending axis is not called out
With `LINES=40` alone the player is told `LINES/COLUMNS make it 100x40` and to unset "them", though only one exists in their environment. Worse in the mixed case: pane 100x30 with `COLUMNS=80 LINES=40` prints `Terminal is 100x30 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 80x40.`, where the reader's eye lands on 80 < 100 and has to work out that the problem is 40 > 30. `pinned()` already knows which variable is set, so the notice could name just that one. Also, nothing in either line says these are environment variables — for a player who does not already know, "unset them" is not an action. Naming them singly ("Unset COLUMNS and start again to get the panels.") fixes both at once.

### 5. nit, no change requested — the exact gate costs the panels for a one-over pin that still worked
Measured on a pristine `main` build in a scratch copy: `COLUMNS=101` in a 100-column pane loses only the right border column (panels, coordinates and status all intact), and `LINES=31` in a 30-row pane draws the whole layout correctly with only the invisible bottom row lost. Those two now fall back to classic. I would still keep the strict gate — the rule is simple, the doc states it, and clamping curses to the window would be undone at the first resize since ncurses re-derives the pinned dimension (the argument already written at `tui.c:1209-1218` about not overriding "a size somebody set on purpose"). Worth knowing that the boundary is not free, not worth softening.

### On your explicit questions

- **Is the notice intelligible?** Line 2 carries it; line 1 is the weak half, and finding 4 is the cheapest improvement — naming the single variable that is actually set turns jargon into an instruction. Comparing against the other three, the outcome gap in finding 3 is the more visible inconsistency.
- **Refusing versus drawing clipped:** refusing is right, and the `LINES` case is the strongest evidence for it rather than the weakest. On `main` at `LINES=40` in a 20-row pane I saw exactly what you did after six `status` commands, and the reason it cannot be lived with is that the damage is unrecoverable: curses clips rows off the bottom and cannot reflow them when the window grows (the #166 note at `tui.c:965-972`), so a player who "thought it was working" loses the conversation permanently, in a mode whose whole promise is that the conversation scrolls under fixed panels. Taking a display that looks usable for the first minute is the right trade.
- **Boundary:** verified at ±1 on both axes and at equality; behaves exactly as the diff describes.

## What I exercised

Built `debug` on the branch and a pristine `main` in a scratch copy for before/after comparison. All TUI work on a private socket (`tmux -f /dev/null -L uirev`), killed only sessions I created, no stdout redirection in any pane.

- New notice at 100x30/`COLUMNS=190`, 100x20/`LINES=40`, 100x30/`COLUMNS=80 LINES=40`, and 40x24/`COLUMNS=80` (wraps mid-word at 40 columns, same as the existing 57-column notices — not counted as a finding).
- Boundary: `COLUMNS` 99/100/101 in a 100x30 pane; `LINES` 29/30/31 in the same. Panels at 99 and 100, refusal at 101; same on rows.
- Recovery: pinned `COLUMNS=190`, pane grown to 190x30, `play again` → panels come up, no spurious notice.
- Play-again journeys: pinned oversize with no resize (correctly silent); with a height resize; with a width resize; and the too-small-then-grown sequence that produces the contradictory message in finding 1. Each played `regular/short/novice`, a name, `quit`, then `y`.
- Regression baselines: 80x24 and 72x24 with nothing pinned (panels normal), piped `-t` (`Full-screen mode needs a terminal`), and a deterministic plain-mode journey (`tournament 42`, `srscan`/`status`/`chart`/`quit`) diffed byte-for-byte against `main` — identical, 81 lines.
- Read `sst.doc:1541-1585` and `README.md:95-125` against the behavior above.

- `LINES=40` in a 20-row pane: the panels draw fine — they cap at `PANELH` — but the message window's lower rows are off the bottom, so the conversation walks off screen. After six `status` commands the last visible row read ` COMMAND> t     7.00`: a prompt on top of half a status line.

Neither is the clipping the manual promises for a small terminal.

**Now the game refuses and plays classic**, with a notice of its own:

```
Terminal is 100x30 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 190x30.
Unset them and start again to get the panels.
```

52 columns and 45 at three-digit sizes, both measured, inside the 57 the other notices hold. It is deliberately different advice from the too-small pair, which says to grow the window: growing does not help here, and neither does answering yes at "play again", because nothing in a session can unset an exported variable.

**A pinned dimension smaller than the window is deliberately left alone** — the panels are then drawn narrow or short with room to spare, which works, and refusing it would take the display from anyone whose profile exports a `COLUMNS` that happens to be right. Verified: `COLUMNS=80` in a 140x36 pane still brings the panels up at 80.

## What I checked myself

- Full `tests/tui.sh` → `tui OK`, including the two new `fallback` cases and the `env size:` and `one pinned:` cases from #165.
- Plain mode byte-identical over a deterministic two-game journey, 81 lines.
- 80x24 and 72x24 draw normally — the new gate cannot fire when nothing is pinned, since curses' size is then the terminal's.

## What I want from you

- **The new notice, as a player reads it.** Is "LINES/COLUMNS make it 190x30" intelligible to someone who does not know what those are? The second line tells them what to do; the first is trying to explain why. Compare it against the three notices already there.
- **Whether refusing is the right answer at all**, versus drawing something clipped. My argument is that the classic display fits any window and a wrapped frame does not, but you are the one who judges what a player would rather have.
- **The boundary**: a pinned size exactly equal to the window, and one a single row or column over. The gate is `LINES > ws_row || COLS > ws_col`.
- **The `LINES=40` case specifically** — the panels looked fine there at first glance and only went wrong as the conversation grew, so a player might reasonably think it was working. Does refusing at startup feel right, or does it take away a display that looked usable?
- Anything the earlier rounds on this machinery did not reach.

Same constraints: private tmux socket via `-L <yourname>` with `-f /dev/null`, never a bare `kill-server`, never `kill-session` on a session you did not create, scratch directory with a copy of `sst.doc`, never redirect the game's stdout in the pane.

Read-only: report findings, never edit.

content.text:
## Verdict

The core decision is right and the new startup notice reads well: I reproduced both failure modes on `main` (at `COLUMNS=190`/100-col pane the frame runs off the edge; at `LINES=40`/20-row pane the conversation walks off the bottom until the last visible row was literally ` COMMAND> t     7.00`), and the branch replaces both with a classic display that fits the window, a two-line notice inside the 57-column budget the other notices hold, and an exact boundary that behaves as documented (pinned == window draws panels, +1 refuses, pinned smaller still draws). **It needs changes before commit**, though, for one thing the change introduces and does not cover: the *between-games* retry notice now quotes the pinned size and contradicts itself — a player who does exactly what the too-small notice asked is told `Terminal is 190x30 -- need 72x24, staying classic.` The documentation also asserts something the retry path does not do, and states the old "the panels come up at the pinned size" claim two sentences before retracting it.

## Findings

### 1. should-fix (I considered blocker) — the play-again retry notice now tells the player a size their window does not have, and a requirement they already exceed
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.c:571-583` (the `tui_refused_size()` branch) is unchanged, but this branch makes it newly reachable with an *oversize* refusal behind it, so `refusedcols`/`refusedlines` now carry curses' inflated number.

Reproduced, two ways, both starting from a notice the game itself printed:

- Pane 100x20, `COLUMNS=190`. Startup: `Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display.` / `Grow the terminal to 72x24 and the next game gets panels.` Player grows the pane to 100x30 — exactly what was asked — answers `y`, and gets:
  `Terminal is 190x30 -- need 72x24, staying classic.`
- Pane 100x20, `LINES=40`. Startup: the new notice. Player widens to 120x20, answers `y`:
  `Terminal is 120x40 -- need 72x24, staying classic.` (their window is 120x**20**.)

What a player experiences: a size that is not their terminal's, a stated requirement of 72x24 that the quoted size plainly clears, and no mention of `LINES`/`COLUMNS` at all — so no way forward. On `main` this string could never carry a pinned oversize number (the oversize case brought the panels up instead), so it is this change that opens the path. It also falsifies the new doc sentence "the game says both sizes and plays classic instead", which is true only of the startup path.

Suggestion: ask `tui_refused_oversize()` in the retry branch too and print the pinned-size wording there (the same two lines, or a one-line form such as `Terminal is 120x20 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 120x40.`), falling through to `Terminal is %dx%d -- need 72x24, staying classic.` only for a genuinely too-small window. The startup path already has exactly the right sentence; the retry path just needs to reach it.

### 2. should-fix — the manual states the superseded behavior, then retracts it two sentences later
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/README.md:110-120` and `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/sst.doc:1563-1571` still say "...if that carries the measurement past 72x24 the panels come up at the pinned size rather than your window's", and then "Pinned larger they would not fit the screen at all, so the game says both sizes and plays classic instead." A reader takes the first claim, then has to unlearn it. Suggestion: make the middle sentence conditional — e.g. "...and if that carries the measurement past 72x24 the game looks at whether the pinned size fits your window" — so the pinned-smaller and pinned-larger sentences that follow each complete it rather than one contradicting it.

### 3. should-fix (small) — the new notice is the only fallback that does not say what display you are getting
The three existing notices all name the outcome: "using the classic display" (twice) and "staying classic". The new pair says what is wrong and what to do, and then the game simply starts classic:

```
Terminal is 100x30 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 190x30.
Unset them and start again to get the panels.
```

A player can infer it from "to get the panels", but the established shape here is outcome line + action line, and this one is diagnosis + action. Suggestion, both within budget: keep line 1 and make line 2 `Using the classic display; unset them and start again.` (54 columns), or keep line 2 as-is and end line 1 with the outcome if you can spare the width. Either keeps the deliberate "start again", not "resize", advice you were after.

### 4. nit — "LINES/COLUMNS ... them" when only one is pinned, and the offending axis is not called out
With `LINES=40` alone the player is told `LINES/COLUMNS make it 100x40` and to unset "them", though only one exists in their environment. Worse in the mixed case: pane 100x30 with `COLUMNS=80 LINES=40` prints `Terminal is 100x30 but LINES/COLUMNS make it 80x40.`, where the reader's eye lands on 80 < 100 and has to work out that the problem is 40 > 30. `pinned()` already knows which variable is set, so the notice could name just that one. Also, nothing in either line says these are environment variables — for a player who does not already know, "unset them" is not an action. Naming them singly ("Unset COLUMNS and start again to get the panels.") fixes both at once.

### 5. nit, no change requested — the exact gate costs the panels for a one-over pin that still worked
Measured on a pristine `main` build in a scratch copy: `COLUMNS=101` in a 100-column pane loses only the right border column (panels, coordinates and status all intact), and `LINES=31` in a 30-row pane draws the whole layout correctly with only the invisible bottom row lost. Those two now fall back to classic. I would still keep the strict gate — the rule is simple, the doc states it, and clamping curses to the window would be undone at the first resize since ncurses re-derives the pinned dimension (the argument already written at `tui.c:1209-1218` about not overriding "a size somebody set on purpose"). Worth knowing that the boundary is not free, not worth softening.

### On your explicit questions

- **Is the notice intelligible?** Line 2 carries it; line 1 is the weak half, and finding 4 is the cheapest improvement — naming the single variable that is actually set turns jargon into an instruction. Comparing against the other three, the outcome gap in finding 3 is the more visible inconsistency.
- **Refusing versus drawing clipped:** refusing is right, and the `LINES` case is the strongest evidence for it rather than the weakest. On `main` at `LINES=40` in a 20-row pane I saw exactly what you did after six `status` commands, and the reason it cannot be lived with is that the damage is unrecoverable: curses clips rows off the bottom and cannot reflow them when the window grows (the #166 note at `tui.c:965-972`), so a player who "thought it was working" loses the conversation permanently, in a mode whose whole promise is that the conversation scrolls under fixed panels. Taking a display that looks usable for the first minute is the right trade.
- **Boundary:** verified at ±1 on both axes and at equality; behaves exactly as the diff describes.

## What I exercised

Built `debug` on the branch and a pristine `main` in a scratch copy for before/after comparison. All TUI work on a private socket (`tmux -f /dev/null -L uirev`), killed only sessions I created, no stdout redirection in any pane.

- New notice at 100x30/`COLUMNS=190`, 100x20/`LINES=40`, 100x30/`COLUMNS=80 LINES=40`, and 40x24/`COLUMNS=80` (wraps mid-word at 40 columns, same as the existing 57-column notices — not counted as a finding).
- Boundary: `COLUMNS` 99/100/101 in a 100x30 pane; `LINES` 29/30/31 in the same. Panels at 99 and 100, refusal at 101; same on rows.
- Recovery: pinned `COLUMNS=190`, pane grown to 190x30, `play again` → panels come up, no spurious notice.
- Play-again journeys: pinned oversize with no resize (correctly silent); with a height resize; with a width resize; and the too-small-then-grown sequence that produces the contradictory message in finding 1. Each played `regular/short/novice`, a name, `quit`, then `y`.
- Regression baselines: 80x24 and 72x24 with nothing pinned (panels normal), piped `-t` (`Full-screen mode needs a terminal`), and a deterministic plain-mode journey (`tournament 42`, `srscan`/`status`/`chart`/`quit`) diffed byte-for-byte against `main` — identical, 81 lines.
- Read `sst.doc:1541-1585` and `README.md:95-125` against the behavior above.

Unset COLUMNS and start again -- classic for now.

Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display.

```

Both facts, one cycle, no false promise. (Reordering the two checks in `tui_init()` also works but reads worse — it would tell a genuinely 20-row window about environment variables first.)

**3. nit — "start again" collides with the question the player just answered.** `sst.c:587`.

Pane 100x20 with `COLUMNS=190`, grown to 100x22 (still short), answer `y`:

Terminal is 190x22 -- need 72x24, staying classic.
```

**5. nit — the new refusal is missing from the canonical "why `-t` went classic" lists.** `README.md:95-100`, `sst.doc:1547-1550`.

Both enumerate the reasons full-screen mode is not possible — too small, no terminal, `TERM` cannot address the cursor — and neither mentions a pinned size bigger than the window, even though that notice now fires at *startup* with no resize involved. One clause in each list — "or an exported `LINES`/`COLUMNS` is bigger than the window" — closes it.

I convinced myself it is unreachable — `resize_term()` at `tui.c:1252` forces `LINES`/`COLS` to the ioctl size when nothing is pinned, so the oversize test cannot fire — but only failure of `resize_term()` stands between that comment's "which no caller should reach" and a garbled sentence.
